jobs.description:
What You Will Do

This position will be filled at either the Science/Engineering Program Manager 4 or 5 level, depending on the skills and experience of the selected candidate. Exceptional candidates may be considered for a higher-level position, and additional job responsibilities will be assigned if the candidate is hired at the higher level.

The Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) Global Security (GS) Directorate is seeking applicants for the Program Manager (PM) of the Joint Space Protection (JSP) Program. This position reports directly to the Program Directors for Intelligence and Emerging Threats (GS-IET) and National Security and Defense (GS-NSD).

The JSP provides space and ground solutions for Department of War (DOW) and Intelligence Community (IC) customer needs. These projects range from concept studies to data processing tools to spaceflight hardware. The JSP is currently executing ~$40M of projects in FY2026, with significant growth anticipated in FY2027. Note that DOW activities associated with the United States Nuclear Detonation Detection System (USNDS) are led by the Nuclear Nonproliferation and Security Program Office (GS-NNS).

Science/Engineering Program Manager 4 ($153,600-$266,500)

The PM leads the management, coordination, and development of JSP space activities and will serve as LANL's principal interface to the IC and DOW for all space related activities in coordination with the GS Program Directors and the GS Executive Advisor. The selected candidate will also advise Program Directors, Line Managers and internal investment boards (such as Laboratory-Directed Research and Development - LDRD) on the needs and opportunities of customer-funded space programs.

The JSP PM will coordinate with other LANL Program offices which conduct space activities as needed to set institutional priorities, resolve resource conflicts, and ensure coherent investments across the LANL space enterprise.

Science/Engineering Program Manager 5 ($184,200-$329,700)

In addition to what was outlined at the lower level, at this level the JSP PM will identify and coordinate strategic partnerships with other Federally Funded Research and Development Corporations (FFRDCs) and Commercial Industry to leverage LANL's unique capabilities for system development. This work will include collaboration with other LANL organizations, such as the Feynman Center for Innovation (FCI) to address legal aspects of collaboration.

What You Need

Minimum Job Requirements:

Technical Knowledge
: Demonstrated experience in space system design, production, and/or operations including a working familiarity with NASA and/or DOW Technical Readiness Level (TRL) assessment as it applies to space systems. The Program Manager is not expected to be an expert in all areas of space system design and operations but is expected to be conversant in critical areas and knowledgeable of integration and test.

Project Management:
Demonstrated ability to convert concepts and strategic objectives into executable projects with measurable outcomes. Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while balancing priorities and deadlines. Familiarity with coordinating interdisciplinary efforts and aligning project work with broader organizational goals. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail in both planning and execution.

Customer Relations and Stakeholder Engagement
: Ability to build effective working relationships with both internal and external stakeholders. Experience collaborating with leadership, subject matter experts, partner organizations, and/or public audiences. Ability to assess customer needs and translate them into achievable projects scopes and deliverables. Experience setting realistic expectations regarding project scope, timelines, resources, and deliverables.

Leadership
: Demonstrated peer-leadership ability to collaborate and strategize with colleagues to meet customer/project objectives while developing team members and meeting institutional goals.

Teamwork/Collaboration
: Demonstrated ability to foster a respectful, collaborative, and productive work environment. Ability to work constructively and professionally with colleagues across disciplines and backgrounds. Experience mentoring staff and supporting professional development. Willingness to share knowledge, provide constructive feedback, and support team success.

In addition to the duties outlined above, the Science/Engineering Program Manager 5 is expected to:

Technical Knowledge
: Demonstrated subject matter expertise in space system design, production, and/or operations. A SEPM 5 should be able to draw from past leadership experience of space system design, production, and/or operations.

Project Management:
Experience bringing projects through formal systems engineering reviews (e.g. SRR, PDR, CDR) including negotiating the content of these reviews with sponsors.

Customer Relations and Stakeholder Engagement:
Experience engaging with senior sponsors at the GS-15 level and above.

Education/Experience for Science/Engineering Program Manager 4:
Position requires a bachelor's degree in a science or engineering related field from an accredited institution and 12 years of directly related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience directly related to the occupation. At this level an advanced degree is typically expected. An advanced degree in a science or engineering field is preferred.

Education/Experience for Science/Engineering Program Manager 5:
Position requires a bachelor's degree in a science or engineering related field from an accredited institution and 15 years of directly related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience directly related to the occupation. At this level an advanced degree is typically expected. An advanced degree in a science or engineering field is preferred.

Desired Qualifications:

Expert knowledge of at least one of the following: space system hardware/software development, space ground system development, and/or space system operations.
Commercial or Government certification in program management, test, and/or systems engineering.
Functional understanding of Space Domain Awareness (SDA) and the roles of various US Government agencies in SDA.
Experience with the US DOW and/or IC space programs.
Active DOE Q clearance

Note to Applicants:

For full consideration, applicants must submit a comprehensive cover letter that addresses all the minimum requirements of the position.

Work Environment:

Work Location:
The work location for this position is onsite and located in Los Alamos, NM. All work locations are at the discretion of management.

Position commitment:
Regular appointment employees are required to serve a period of continuous service in their current position in order to be eligible to apply for posted jobs throughout the Laboratory. If an employee has not served the time required, they may only apply for Laboratory jobs with the documented approval of their Division Leader. The position commitment for this position is 1 year.

Note to Applicants:

Due to federal restrictions contained in the current National Defense Authorization Act, citizens of the People's Republic of China-including the special administrative regions of Hong Kong and Macau-as well as citizens of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea), and the Russian Federation, who are not Lawful Permanent Residents ("green card" holders) are prohibited from accessing facilities that support the mission, functions, and operations of national security laboratories and nuclear weapons production facilities, which includes Los Alamos National Laboratory. Where You Will Work

Located in beautiful northern New Mexico, Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is a multidisciplinary research institution engaged in strategic science on behalf of national security. Our generous benefits package includes:

PPO or High Deductible medical insurance with the same large nationwide network
Dental and vision insurance
Free basic life and disability insurance
Paid childbirth and parental leave
Award-winning 401(k) (6% matching plus 3.5% annually)
Learning opportunities and tuition assistance
Flexible schedules and time off (PTO and holidays)

Extensive relocation packages (outside a 50 mile radius)

Receipt of a Q clearance and additional access authorization ultimately is a decision of the Federal Government and not of Triad.

Eligibility requirements: To obtain a clearance, an individual must be at least 18 years of age; U.S. citizenship is required except in very limited circumstances. See DOE Order 472.2 for additional information.

A positive drug test for marijuana will result in termination of employment, even if the use was pre-offer.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
About Rewards Network

For 41 years, Rewards Network has been helping restaurants grow revenue, increase traffic, and boost customer engagement through innovative financial, marketing services, and premier dining rewards programs. By offering unique card-linked offers, we introduce diners to fantastic restaurant experiences, leveraging advanced technology and data analytics to deliver value to restaurants, diners, and our strategic partners' loyalty programs.

Our Culture

At Rewards Network, you'll be part of a driven and diverse team that excels in collaboration, issue resolution, and taking ownership of both personal growth and the company's success. We take pride in partnering with the world's most powerful loyalty programs to drive full-price paying customers to local restaurants through marketing services and flexible funding options. Our engaging and rewarding environment is designed to help you gain your full potential.

Job Overview

The Senior Technical Program Manager at Rewards Network owns the planning, governance, and delivery of the company's most complex, strategic programs — including large-scale product transformations on our consumer- and restaurant-facing sides of the business, major product modernization initiatives (from discovery through launch), large-scale partner and restaurant onboarding programs, new strategic partner and payments integrations, and core payments infrastructure upgrades and migrations. Each of these spans multiple concurrent workstreams across Product, Engineering, Data, Partner Management, Marketing, and Operations. This role owns the end-to-end timeline, success, and delivery health of that program portfolio — from Conception through launch — establishing the operating rhythm and managing cross-program dependencies, risk, and stakeholder communication so Rewards Network's highest-priority initiatives land on time, meet a standard of greatness, and align with business objectives.

This is an embedded owner into the cross-functional team: someone senior enough to operate without handholding, deep enough in the details of the work to know why each program matters (not just its next milestone), and comfortable reporting credibly in both directions — upward (to executives and senior leaders) with clean, balanced, actionable updates, and outward (to Partners, Ops, Marketing, and Engineering) to ensure alignment. This role reports directly to the Senior Director of Product and is an experienced individual contributor role for someone who thrives at the intersection of rigorous program governance and cross-functional influence at the executive level.

This is a hybrid position that requires in office presence 3 days a week (Tuesday-Thursday) in Chicago.

What you’ll bring to the table: (Responsibilities)

Own end-to-end program management for Rewards Network's most complex, cross-functional strategic initiatives — spanning platform transformations, product modernization efforts, large-scale partner and merchant onboarding, new partner and payments integrations, and core payments infrastructure upgrades — often managing several concurrently.
Define and maintain program plans, timelines, milestones, and cross-program dependency maps; drive accountability against committed dates and quality bars.
Proactively identify, track, and mitigate risks and issues; escalate appropriately and recommend trade-offs when scope, schedule, or resources require rebalancing.
Work with Product leadership to ensure the right work is sequenced against available resources. Establish and run the governance operating model — steering committees, working-team cadences, and review rhythms — to keep each program's health visible without active leadership involvement.
Own program-level reporting and status communication to executives, senior leadership, and key stakeholders; translate complex delivery details across multiple concurrent programs into simple, clear, decision-ready summaries.
Manage cross-program dependencies with internal partners and external integrations (e.g., loyalty program partners); ensure alignment on requirements, timelines, and acceptance criteria across every program in the portfolio.
Own the cross-functional execution of product launches and go-to-market plans: coordinate readiness, dependencies, timing, and stakeholder alignment across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Legal, Finance, and Partner Management. Partner closely with Marketing on positioning and messaging, but owns the plan, the timeline, and an on-time, successful delivery.
Serve as the primary point of contact and connective tissue for cross-functional programs — this includes applying pressure (or escalation) to other leaders as needed to keep programs on-track.
Continuously improve program management practices, tools, templates, and governance processes, including eliciting feedback on how we can continue to improve them.
Leverage AI tools and workflows to increase program management velocity and quality — accelerating status synthesis, risk analysis, and plan generation — and model AI-native practices for the broader cross-functional team.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - IT Services
jobs.description:
About Us:
At Booking.com, data drives our decisions. Technology is at our core. And innovation is everywhere. But our company is more than datasets, lines of code or A/B tests. We’re the thrill of the first night in a new place. The excitement of the next morning. The friends you encounter. The journeys you take. The sights you see. And the memories you make. Through our products, partners and people, we make it easier for everyone to experience the world.

About the team:
Booking.com IT Services size and technical complexity require specialists who can drive cross-organisational initiatives with significant technology dependencies. As a Technical Program Manager, you will lead delivery from problem framing through implementation and measurable outcome. You will work directly with engineering, product and operational stakeholders to establish scope, ownership, realistic plans, delivery rhythms and decision-making. You will bring an independent view of progress, surface risk early and help teams make practical trade-offs without adding unnecessary process.

This is an individual-contributor role. It does not include people management. The role may support global services and stakeholders, but its organisational delivery scope is calibrated to TPM rather than Senior TPM.

About the role:
You will independently lead the delivery of technically complex, cross-team initiatives that solve business and internal-customer problems. Working across several engineering and product teams, typically within one track or product group, you will translate an end-to-end technical solution into a realistic program structure, align priorities and ownership, and deliver incremental, measurable value for Booking.com employees and internal customers.

Who you work with

Internal stakeholders

You will work continuously with engineering, product, operations, security, privacy and business teams across Booking.com and relevant Booking Holdings functions. The role requires cooperation, persuasion and clear information-sharing to align priorities and deliver outcomes.

External stakeholders

You may work frequently with technology and service vendors, using clear requirements, delivery plans, risk ownership and performance expectations to support program outcomes.

Role accountability

This is an individual-contributor role with no direct people-management or P&L responsibility. Programs may support globally distributed teams and services, while the organisational delivery scope remains aligned with a TPM role: normally several teams within a track or product group. Decisions and outcomes typically influence the short-to-mid-term delivery horizon.

Perhaps in the "what you bring" mentioning expertise of different delivery methodologies (such as Agile and Lean)?

Key Job Responsibilities And Duties

Lead small-to-medium, technically complex programs and cross-team initiatives with meaningful business or internal-customer impact, normally spanning several teams within a track or product group.
Translate business and internal-customer problems, technical designs and non-functional requirements into a clear delivery structure, milestones and iterative value slices.
Create and maintain realistic, outcome-based plans using relevant delivery and operational metrics.
Clarify decision rights, ownership and accountability across workstreams; make dependencies and the critical path visible.
Identify and manage technical and delivery risks, issues and changes; define mitigation plans (after discussing options with the right owners)
Build alignment across engineering, product, security, privacy, operations and business stakeholders, influencing without formal authority.
Communicate concise program updates and decisions at the right level of detail, including to Director-level stakeholders.
Establish fit-for-purpose governance and delivery practices that work across teams with different ways of working.
Use retrospectives, delivery data and feedback to improve predictability, quality and team collaboration.
Contribute practical learning and reusable delivery practices to the TPM craft community.
Define and maintain program documentation, ensure functional and non-functional requirements are captured, and partner with engineering teams so supporting technical documentation is produced and maintained.
Drive the planning, documentation and communication of strategic programs with leaders across Booking.com and, where relevant, Booking Holdings.

What success looks like

Teams understand the outcome, their ownership and how their work connects to the end-to-end solution.
Plans are credible, continuously updated and focused on incremental value rather than activity alone.
Risks, dependencies and priority conflicts are visible early and have clear owners and decisions.
Stakeholders receive concise, evidence-based information and can make timely trade-offs.
Programs deliver measurable business, employee, reliability, security, cost or operational outcomes.
Delivery practices become simpler and more effective without creating unnecessary governance.

Role Qualifications And Requirements

5+ years of relevant experience in product, project, program or technical program management, working directly with engineering or software-development teams to build, implement or launch technical solutions.
Evidence of personally leading an end-to-end technical program lifecycle: discovery, scope, planning, execution, release or implementation, outcome measurement and learning.
Technical fluency sufficient to understand and explain system components, interfaces, data flows, functional and non-functional requirements, testing or release approaches, failure modes and trade-offs.
Strong delivery-management capability, including iterative planning, sequencing, dependency management, critical-path awareness, risk and issue management, and useful progress metrics.
Ability to align stakeholders and influence decisions without authority, including when teams have competing priorities.
Clear written, verbal and visual communication; able to adapt detail and framing for engineers, managers and Directors.
A data-informed, customer-oriented and pragmatic approach to navigating ambiguity, solving problems and making decisions.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong business awareness and technical vision.
Curiosity and ability to understand architectural and technical aspects of programs and their long-term consequences.
Expertise of different delivery methodologies (such as Agile and Lean)

Preferred Context

Cloud infrastructure, SaaS business applications or DevOps practices.
Identity and access management, including platforms such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or Ping Identity; networking, remote access or internal-platform services.
Programs serving internal customers, including work with vendors or distributed teams.
Programming or engineering background; business-continuity, regulatory or compliance exposure.
Jira, Jira Align or comparable planning and delivery tooling.

AI affinity and mindset

Show curiosity and practical understanding of AI tools and how they can improve work, not just generic enthusiasm.
Demonstrate safe AI habits: awareness of hallucinations, privacy, data handling, corporate guardrails, and the need to validate outputs.
Identify relevant AI use cases for AV/VC operations, such as incident summarisation, log analysis, monitoring insights, knowledge discovery, vendor documentation analysis, meeting room issue triage, runbook generation, and support workflow automation.
Be able to set context-rich prompts, refine outputs, and validate AI-generated work before using it in operational or stakeholder-facing decisions.
Actively encourage responsible AI adoption in the team, while avoiding overclaiming what AI can do or replacing human judgment with unchecked AI output.

Benefits & Perks - Global Impact, Personal Relevance:

Booking.com’s Total Rewards Philosophy is not only about compensation but also about benefits. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, as well unique-to-Booking.com benefits which include:

Annual paid time off and generous paid leave scheme including: parent, grandparent, bereavement, and care leave
Hybrid working including flexible working arrangements, and up to 20 days per year working from abroad (home country)
Industry leading product discounts - up to 1400 per year - for yourself, including automatic Genius Level 3 status and Booking.com wallet credit
Living and working in Amsterdam, one of the most cosmopolitan cities in Europe
Contributing to a high scale, complex, world renowned product and seeing real-time impact of your work on millions of travelers worldwide
Working in a fast-paced and performance driven culture
Opportunity to utilize technical expertise, leadership capabilities and entrepreneurial spirit
Promote and drive impactful and innovative engineering solutions
Technical, behavioral and interpersonal competence advancement via on-the-job opportunities, experimental projects, hackathons, conferences and active community participation
Competitive compensation and benefits package and some great added perks of working in the home city of Booking.com

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) at Booking.com:

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion have been a core part of our company culture since day one. This ongoing journey starts with our very own employees, who represent over 140 nationalities and a wide range of ethnic and social backgrounds, genders and sexual orientations.

Take it from our Chief People Officer, Paulo Pisano: “At Booking.com, the diversity of our people doesn’t just build an outstanding workplace, it also creates a better and more inclusive travel experience for everyone. Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do. It’s a place where you can make your mark and have a real impact in travel and tech.”

We ensure that colleagues with disabilities are provided the adjustments and tools they need to participate in the job application and interview process, to perform crucial job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

Application Process:

This role does not come with relocation assistance.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. Telecommunications Engineering Degree

IT systems, expertise, and experience are central to Asana's mission of helping teams work together effortlessly. As an IT Technical Program Manager, you'll be a force multiplier across IT and Asana's cross-functional business partners. You will drive outcomes, programs, and operational rhythms that make IT highly effective and visible outside its own walls. IT TPM work is rarely IT-only: you'll be leading projects, programs, and processes that reach into Security, Product, Workplace, PeopleOps, Legal, and other business lines as a matter of course, not exception.

You'll join the team as a TPM, reporting to the IT TPM function lead, and take ownership of a dynamic portfolio of IT programs and projects. This is a high-autonomy role for someone who wants real ownership early: you'll be trusted to run point on your portfolio while helping shape how the broader IT TPM function operates.

This role is based in our San Francisco office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements.

What You'll Achieve

Lead high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that span organizational boundaries. From IT infrastructure and AI adoption efforts to company-wide strategic initiatives in collaboration with Security, Product, Workplace, PeopleOps, Legal, and other partners.
Own your share of IT's process portfolio. You will fully own one or more highly visible IT processes and influence the development of all TPM processes. Throughout, you will maintain a focus on adaptation and continual improvement.
Run point on program communications. Keep stakeholders aligned, unblock teams, and build durable partnerships within and beyond IT.
Identify, manage, and mitigate risks and dependencies, ensuring alignment across key stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes.
Promote and evolve project management practice across IT. Create repeatable processes that leverage TPM best practices across the organization.
Drive adoption of policies, practices, and procedures across IT and Asana more broadly, through influence and tactful education rather than authority.
Bring a holistic view of the IT ecosystem to design and planning decisions, so solutions support our strategy and day to day operations.
Document and share knowledge so that processes and decisions are legible and repeatable by others, not dependent on any one person.
Help define how the TPM function operates. Partner with your manager to shape the team’s operating model, planning cadences, and processes.

About You

6+ years of program management experience, with meaningful time working in or alongside IT organizations.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams through complex, ambiguous, multi-stakeholder work with only high-level direction. You are comfortable creating structure rather than waiting for it.
Strong grasp of business drivers, with the judgment to align processes to impact, design workable solutions, and implement improvements rather than defaulting to how it's always been done.
Comfortable operating with high autonomy across multiple concurrent workstreams, stakeholders, and timelines.
Excellent written and verbal communication. You enjoy distilling complex or ambiguous issues into actionable plans and can communicate clearly up, down, and across.
Demonstrates curiosity about AI tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage them to enhance productivity, collaboration, or decision-making.
You know when to solve a problem yourself and when to bring in the right partner. Your title history matters less than how you think and how you work with people.
Experience across IT domains: IT Infrastructure, Identity & Access, Networking, Automations & Support.
PMP or ITIL certification.

What We’ll Offer

Our comprehensive compensation package plays a big part in how we recognize you for the impact you have on our path to achieving our mission. We believe that compensation should be reflective of the value you create relative to the market value of your role. To ensure pay is fair and not impacted by biases, we're committed to looking at market value which is why we check ourselves and conduct a yearly pay equity audit.

For this role, the estimated base salary range is between $194,000–$220,000. The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. The listed range above is a guideline, and the base salary range for this role may be modified.

In addition to base salary, your compensation package may include additional components such as equity, sales incentive pay (for most sales roles), and benefits. If you're interviewing for this role, speak with your recruiter to learn more about the total compensation and benefits for this role.

Mental health, wellness & fitness benefits
Career coaching & support
Inclusive family building benefits
Long-term savings or retirement plans
In-office culinary options to cater to your dietary preferences

These are just some of the benefits we offer, and benefits may vary based on role, country, and local regulations. If you're interviewing for this role, speak with your recruiter to learn more about the total compensation and benefits for this role.

Asana is a leading platform for human + AI collaboration. Millions of teams around the world rely on Asana to achieve their most important goals, faster. Asana has been named to Fortune's Best Workplaces for 7+ years and recognized by Fast Company, Forbes, and Gartner for excellence in workplace culture and innovation. jobs.description:
About The Role

Riverbend Energetics is seeking an experienced Program Manager II to lead and execute complex defense programs involving energetic components, electric/stab detonators, and CAD/PAD systems for U.S. defense customers. In this role, you will serve as the primary customer interface and internal program champion, driving program performance across cost, schedule, and technical objectives. This is a high-visibility opportunity to shape mission-critical programs that directly support U.S. national defense.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned defense program customers, managing relationships with program offices, prime contractors, and government agencies throughout the program lifecycle
Lead Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and finance to execute programs on time and within budget
Develop, maintain, and report on program plans, schedules, budgets, and Earned Value Management (EVM) metrics to internal leadership and external customers
Identify, assess, and actively mitigate program risks and opportunities, maintaining formal risk registers and presenting status at program and executive reviews
Manage Contract Data Requirements Lists (CDRLs) and ensure timely, compliant delivery of all contractual deliverables
Support proposal development activities including work breakdown structure (WBS) development, basis-of-estimate (BOE) generation, and schedule development for new business pursuits
Partner with business development and capture teams to support customer calls, program reviews, and organic growth opportunities within existing program portfolios

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or a related technical or management discipline
Minimum 5 years of program management experience in the defense industry, including direct ownership of cost, schedule, and technical performance
Demonstrated experience managing U.S. government contracts in a FAR/DFARS environment, including firm-fixed-price (FFP) and cost-type contract vehicles
Proficiency with program scheduling tools (e.g., Microsoft Project) and program performance reporting
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to present program status to senior leadership and government customers
U.S. citizenship required; must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Defense security clearance
Ability to work on-site at Riverbend Energetics facilities in compliance with applicable explosive safety regulations and site security requirements

Preferred Qualifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or Defense Acquisition University (DAU) program management credentials
Experience managing programs involving energetic materials, ordnance, pyrotechnics, or other hazardous or regulated defense hardware
Familiarity with DODIC/NSN systems, MIL-spec requirements, and defense ordnance qualification processes (e.g., HERO, ESD, drop/shock testing)
Active DoD Secret or Top Secret security clearance
Experience with AS9100 or equivalent quality management systems in a defense manufacturing environment
Prior military service or direct experience working within a government program office

What We Offer

Competitive salary and benefits package
The opportunity to lead programs that directly support U.S. warfighter readiness and national security at a specialized, innovative defense manufacturer
A collaborative, mission-driven culture where program managers have meaningful authority and visibility across a 150-person organization
Professional development support including training, certification assistance, and pathways to senior program leadership roles

Key Requirements

Defense Acquisition & Contracting Fluency: Riverbend operates exclusively in the U.S. defense market under FAR/DFARS regulations with FFP and cost-type contracts. A PM who truly understands the government acquisition lifecycle — not just nominally — will move faster, make fewer compliance errors, and build credibility with government program offices. At a 150-person company, there is no large contracts department to backstop a PM who lacks this knowledge.
Cross-Functional Authority Without Direct Control: The PM leads Integrated Product Teams spanning engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and finance — none of whom report directly to them. At a 150-person company, formal authority is limited and influence is everything. A PM who relies on org-chart power will stall programs; one who builds trust and creates accountability across functions will consistently deliver.
Hazardous / Regulated Hardware Program Experience: Energetic components, detonators, and CAD/PAD systems carry unique regulatory, safety, and qualification burdens — HERO, ESD, MIL-spec compliance, explosive safety site plans — that do not exist in standard defense hardware programs. A PM unfamiliar with this environment will underestimate risk, misschedule qualification activities, and create safety or compliance exposure. This is the single biggest differentiator from a generic defense PM.
Customer Relationship Management Under Pressure: The PM is the primary face to government program offices and prime contractors. Defense customers have long memories, and relationships built or damaged at the program level directly affect re-compete positioning and organic growth. At a small, specialized company like Riverbend, losing a key customer relationship is a material business risk — there is no account team to absorb the damage.
Rigorous Risk & Schedule Discipline: Defense energetics programs involve long-lead materials, tightly regulated test sequences, and low-volume, high-consequence deliverables where a single schedule slip can affect warfighter readiness. A PM at Riverbend must maintain formal, credible risk registers and schedules — not as reporting theater, but as actual management tools. In a small company without deep program management infrastructure, the PM must personally enforce this discipline.

About Riverbend Energetics

Riverbend Energetics is a defense and industrial manufacturer based in Alton, IL. We develop and produce energetic materials and specialty munitions for U.S. defense and allied customers. Our mission-critical work demands precision, safety, and a commitment to excellence.

jobs.title: Marketing Business Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Who are we?

At UpGuard, we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

Where does this role fit in?

We are seeking a Marketing Business Operations Manager to own the marketing budget process end-to-end and act as the operational backbone of the marketing team.

This role goes beyond coordination and support, you'll independently design and drive process and systems improvements, own the team's work management platform, and lead change management for new ways of working across marketing.

It's best suited to someone who already operates with real ownership and is ready to bring that judgment to a fast-moving marketing organisation.

What will you do?

Process & Systems Support

Own identification of friction points in how work moves between Marketing teams (shared services and squads), and lead the design and rollout of improvements
Own admin-level configuration and governance of the team's work management platform (Asana), including templates, custom fields, rules, and work structure standards
Lead evaluation and implementation of automation and no-code tooling, including AI tools, to scale the team's capacity
Lead change management for new processes and tools across the marketing team, including initiatives driven by leadership, and support the team through transitions

Budget Ownership & Financial Planning

Own the marketing budget process end-to-end, leading annual planning in partnership with department heads across the marketing organization
Lead the monthly forecasting cycle, reconcile actuals against budget, and proactively surface risks and opportunities to leadership
Build and maintain budget models and dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into spend
Partner with Finance on budget governance, ensuring documentation and reporting standards are met
Oversee vendor invoicing and purchase order processes, resolving escalations as needed

Events & Logistics

Oversee the planning and execution of internal marketing events, including venue and vendor strategy
Oversee travel arrangements and event logistics for the marketing team, resolving complex or escalated issues
Own meeting scheduling and calendar strategy for marketing leadership, including recurring cadences
Facilitate executive meetings, ensuring effective structure, capture decisions and drive follow-through, and follow-through on action items
Own the strategy and vendor relationships for the company's online swag store, including budget and forecasting, and own the internal request process end-to-end.

Tools, Content & Reporting

Own and continuously evolve the marketing team's Notion workspace and team handbooks
Own the marketing team's Asana project, setting best practices for tasks, timelines, and status reporting
Own marketing goal tracking within Asana, partnering with leadership to ensure strategic alignment
Develop and refine presentation materials for quarterly global marketing meetings, incorporating strategic narrative
Own agenda-setting and preparation for key marketing meetings, partnering directly with leadership

What will you bring?

3+ years of experience designing and improving workflows and processes across teams, ideally within a shared-services or squad-based structure
Demonstrated, admin-level experience managing a work management platform (Asana, Monday, or similar)
Strong systems thinking, able to see an operating model holistically, not just optimize individual tools
Proven experience with automation or no-code tooling, including AI tools
Demonstrated change management or facilitation experience, with a track record of driving adoption of new ways of working
Demonstrated experience owning a budget process end-to-end, not just tracking spend
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work confidently with senior stakeholders

What will give you an edge?

Experience specifically within a marketing function, versus a generalist ops/PM background
Data and reporting skills, e.g. building capacity models to identify trends and scaling opportunities
Experience partnering with or managing external vendors and contractors
Experience mentoring or guiding junior team members

What's in it for you?

Monthly Lifestyle subsidy: Use this for financial, physical, and mental well-being
WFH set-up allowance: To ensure you have the right environment to work in, we will help you get set up within your first 3 months at UpGuard
$1500 USD annual Learning & Development allowance: To support your career development, all team members will be able to expense development opportunities against this allowance
Annual leave: PTO plus two additional UpGuardian leave days to give you time to recharge your batteries.
18 weeks paid Parental Leave: Irrespective of parenting role
Personal Leave Allowance: This includes sick & carer’s leave
Fully remote working environment: While we have physical offices in Sydney & Hobart, we do not mandate compulsory attendance
Top-spec hardware: All team members will be provided with top-spec laptops for their role
Generative AI subsidy: UpGuard provides paid subscriptions for all team members to access generative AI tools to support their work

UpGuard is a Certified Great Place to Work® in the US, Australia, UK and India, establishing its position as a leading global technology employer. 99% of team members agree that UpGuard is a great place to work! Apply now to find out why!

Taking ownership of projects/orders following handover from Sales.

Global Sales:

Lead Intelligence Strategy & Support: Act as the primary analytical partner for the Lead Intelligence initiative, helping to define and align lead inventory allocation and optimization across all geographies.
Advanced Forecasting & Modeling: Evolve and improve sophisticated forecasting models for lead delivery and sales pipeline. You will perform scenario analysis to maximize outcomes while optimizing the consumer and client experience.
Inventory & Yield Optimization: Conduct deep-dive analyses to identify and prioritize high-value leads by geography and intent signal. Use these insights to recommend rules-based allocation strategies that optimize yield.

Education & Experience: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Analytics, Math, Economics, or a related field, with 5+ years of experience analyzing data to answer critical business questions. Master’s Degree with 3+ years of experience or PhD also eligible.

Cloud Platforms: Experience working within cloud-based environments such as AWS and Snowflake.
Strategic Thinking: Ability to handle operational complexity and move from “what” the data says to “why” it is moving, enabling data-driven decisioning for the entire organization.
Agility: Comfort working in a highly agile, intensely iterative environment where you must manage multiple priorities and ambiguous concepts.

We balance creativity and innovation on a foundation of in-person collaboration. For most roles, our employees work three or more days in our Austin headquarters, where they have the opportunity to collaborate in-person, adding richness to our culture and knitting us closer together.

Turn complex data into clear, actionable insights that support supervisory decisions and drive meaningful regulatory outcomes

Develop specialist skills in data analytics within a high-profile regulatory environment, building skills and experience that can help protect millions of consumers

We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK.

SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition.

Power your future with Qualus
in our Information Technology department as a Senior Cyber Security Analyst. Cyber Analyst is a vital member of the Qualus IT Security & Compliance team and plays an important role in protecting the organization’s systems, networks, data, and emerging technology platforms through proactive monitoring, detection, and response to cybersecurity threats.

This role requires expertise in enterprise security operations, threat analysis, and governance of modern technology ecosystems, including AI-enabled solutions, ensuring the protection of sensitive data and the resilience of business operations.

The Cyber Analyst will be responsible for monitoring and analyzing security events across Qualus’ layered security architecture, including endpoint, network, email, data protection, and AI-enabled systems and services.

Additionally, the Cyber Analyst will support the secure adoption and governance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions across Qualus, ensuring appropriate controls, data protections, and compliance requirements are enforced.

A security first mindset, strong analytical skills, and the ability to assess risk across both traditional IT systems and AI driven technologies are critical to success in this role.

This position may require after hours support as determined by the needs of the business, including participation in incident response activities.

Responsibilities

Monitor, triage, and investigate alerts across endpoint, identity, email, network, cloud, SIEM/EDR, AI-enabled systems, and data protection platforms.
Correlate security events across Qualus enterprise security stack, including CrowdStrike Falcon Complete, Microsoft Defender, Abnormal Security, Zscaler Z4U, Meraki, Microsoft Purview, Tenable Nessus, and Falcon Next-Gen SIEM/logging platforms.
Support incident response activities, including alert validation, containment coordination, evidence collection, root cause analysis, corrective action tracking, and post-incident documentation.
Support Microsoft security and compliance platforms, including Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Purview, data classification, sensitivity labeling, DLP, retention, audit, and eDiscovery-related activities.
Perform vulnerability management activities using Tenable Nessus and CrowdStrike related processes, including validation, risk prioritization, remediation coordination, exception tracking, and reporting.
Support SIEM/EDR detection engineering, alert tuning, investigation workflows, and security playbook development.
Assist with enforcement of Zero Trust principles, including conditional access, identity-based controls, Federated Authentication (SSO), MFA, RBAC, least privilege, and device posture validation.
Review and support cybersecurity policies, standards, and procedures related to access control, acceptable use, data protection, AI governance, vulnerability management, incident response, and vendor risk management.
Support security assessments for SaaS platforms, cloud services, vendors, and AI-enabled tools to identify risks.
Assist with audit evidence collection, customer security questionnaires, control validation, and compliance documentation aligned with SOC 2, NIST 800-171, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, and other applicable requirements.
Stay current on threat trends, AI security risks, Microsoft security capabilities, data protection practices, and security operations best practices.

Experience with CrowdStrike Falcon, Abnormal Security, Zscaler, Tenable Nessus, Meraki, and Falcon Next Gen SIEM/logging platforms.

Research Analyst

Location:
Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
Salary range:
TZS 7,311,684–9,704,383 gross per month
Application link:
https://form.jotformeu.com/262592084102553

SUMMARY

Laterite is looking for a new Research Analyst with an understanding of data analysis and a strong motivation to work in social and economic research to join our office in Dar es Salaam. This role combines research design, data analysis, project management support, and fieldwork coordination in a collaborative and fast-paced environment.

This position is open exclusively to Tanzanian nationals.

WHO WE ARE

Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others.

We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 90+ full-time staff and more than 2,000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles.

THE ENVIRONMENT YOU’RE STEPPING INTO

You will join our Tanzania team in a high-trust environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won’t be micromanaged here—we want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced field teams, and actively improve the systems you work with.
Laterite was founded in 2010 in Kigali, and our office in Dar es Salaam opened in 2021. Our project portfolio in Tanzania is varied and ranges from data collection (including mixed-methods studies) to full-cycle research projects. The Tanzania team works across all our key sectors with the majority of projects in education, public health and agriculture topics. Our team in Tanzania currently consists of 5 team members.

While based in our Dar es Salaam office, you will support Laterite’s Uganda team, contributing to projects in both countries. The Uganda portfolio is just as varied, combining data collection with full-cycle research studies, and spans the agriculture, public health, education and energy sectors. You will collaborate with the Uganda team remotely.

HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT

1 Supporting research projects

Support the ethical approval process, research design, and development of research instruments.
Conduct quantitative and qualitative data analysis.
Draft sections of reports and presentations for clients.
Support communication with clients and internal project teams on project progress.

2 Contributing to data collection

Code survey instruments using SurveyCTO and other ODK-based platforms.
Collaborate with field teams to develop training materials and support enumerator trainings.
Participate in field visits to understand and improve data collection processes.

3 Strengthening data quality and analysis

Monitor, clean, and validate incoming survey data.
Work closely with field teams to resolve data quality issues.
Support statistical analysis and interpretation of findings.
Contribute to consultancy-quality reports and data-driven insights.

4 Contributing to business development (Optional)

If you are interested, there is also room to contribute to our business development efforts, either through proactive business development or by contributing to the development of technical and financial proposals.

WHAT YOU BRING

We are looking for a colleague with strong quantitative data analysis skills and a motivation to work on socio-economic development research. Specifically, you have:
A completed Master’s degree in Economics, Public Health, Development or related fields.
At least one year of professional experience in similar roles or tasks. (We welcome experience gained through internships, dissertation work, or participation in an academic research group, provided you can demonstrate how this experience meets the requirements of the role.)
Strong quantitative data analysis skills and proficiency in Stata.
Excellent written and oral communication skills in English and Kiswahili.

In addition, we welcome:
Experience working with ODK-based platforms (e.g., SurveyCTO).
Previous work experience in Tanzania.
Organizational and interpersonal skills, self-motivation and drive to work in a collaborative environment.

WHAT YOU’LL LEARN AND DEVELOP

Technical research design, including sampling and impact evaluation methodologies.
Project management and client communication.
Advanced data analysis, statistical techniques, and coding skills.
Report writing and presentation of findings in a consultancy-quality format.

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU

Competitive compensation. TZS 7,311,684 - TZS 9,704,383
gross monthly salary (exact grade determined by experience/interviews), medical insurance, pension contribution, and 21 days of annual leave.
Professional growth.
We are also committed to supporting our staff’s learning, providing an annual learning budget of up to USD 1,000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year.
Flexibility.
We also provide remote work options in accordance with Laterite’s remote work policy.

READY TO BUILD WITH US? NEXT STEPS

Online assessment.
Complete a 30-minute online verbal reasoning and quantitative assessment. No special preparation is required. Link: https://form.jotformeu.com/262592084102553

Application.
Candidates who successfully complete the online assessment will be invited to submit a brief screening questionnaire, along with their CV, through our online application system.
Analytical assessment.
Selected candidates will complete a technical exercise involving statistical analysis using Stata, R, or Python.
Interviews.
Candidates who successfully complete the analytical assessment will be invited to a first interview. The interview stage consists of up to three interviews.

DEADLINE

Applications will be considered on a rolling basis. Details on rolling applications can be found on the website: laterite.com/vacancies.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

Nebius is looking for a highly capable India Supply Chain Security Manager to own and lead all supply chain security operations across India. This role carries full dual-domain responsibility, covering both warehouse and transportation security, making it one of the most comprehensive country-level security mandates within the NGSCS structure.

India represents a strategically significant and operationally complex market within the Nebius supply chain. Its scale, geographic diversity, regulatory environment, and logistics infrastructure present a unique set of security challenges that require a professional with deep local knowledge, strong operational judgment, and the ability to build and manage security standards across a wide network of logistics partners and facilities.

Reporting to the APAC Supply Chain Security Manager, this individual will serve as the primary NGSCS authority for all supply chain security matters in India, establishing vendor relationships, enforcing security standards across warehouse and transportation partners, responding to security incidents, and maintaining full alignment with global NGSCS policies and procedures.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Warehouse Security

Own and lead warehouse security across all facilities in India, with full accountability for facility-level risk and performance
Ensure the secure storage, handling, and integrity of high-value assets across all warehouse and staging facilities in the country
Establish and enforce security requirements acrosslogistics partners operating warehouse and storage facilities, including 3PLs and co-located vendors
Manage physical security standards across facilities, including access control, CCTV, guard force oversight, and alarm systems
Conduct and oversee facility security assessments and audits, benchmarking against TAPA FSR and NGSCS standards
Lead end-to-end response to warehouse security incidents (e.g., theft, loss, unauthorized access, inventory discrepancies), including coordination, investigation, and resolution

Transportation Security

Own and lead transportation security across all shipment lanes within India, with full accountability for in-transit risk and performance
Ensure the secure handling, packaging, and movement of high-value assets across all transportation nodes, from origin to final delivery
Establish and enforce security requirements across transportation partners, including carriers, freight forwarders, and last-mile delivery providers
Conduct risk assessments across transportation routes, handoff points, and carrier operations, and implement effective mitigation strategies
Manage GPS tracking, geofencing, and real-time monitoring of assets across active shipments within India
Lead end-to-end response to in-transit security incidents (e.g., theft, loss, diversion, tampering), including coordination, investigation, and resolution

Country Leadership & Regional Coordination

Serve as the primary NGSCS authority and escalation point for all supply chain security matters in India
Define, implement, and continuously evolve country-level security standards, controls, and procedures aligned with global NGSCS policies
Maintain close coordination with the APAC Supply Chain Security Manager, providing regular visibility into country performance, risks, incidents, and emerging threats
Navigate India's regulatory and compliance landscape, ensuring supply chain security operationsremain aligned with applicable local legal and industry requirements
Monitor and report on country-level security performance, risks, and incidents across both warehouse and transportation domains
Drive continuous improvement of security capabilities across the India vendor andlogistics partner network

Operational Scope

Full country ownership of both warehouse and transportation supply chain security across India, spanning a geographically large and operationally diverse market
Regular engagement with 3PLs, carriers, facility managers, freight forwarders, and security vendorsoperating across India
Travel within Indiarequired for facility site visits, route assessments, partner reviews, and incident response
Operates as part of the broader NGSCS APAC structure, with close coordination with the APAC Supply Chain Security Manager

We Expect You To Have

Minimum 7 years experience in supply chain security, logistics security, or a combined warehouse and transportation security role
Proven experience operating across India, with strong understanding of the local logistics, regulatory, and security environment
Strong experience working with both warehouse and facility security and in-transit transportation security operations
Demonstrated experience working with Indianlogistics providers, 3PLs, carriers, and security vendors
Demonstrated experience leading incident response across warehouse and transportation security events
Familiarity with India's regulatory and compliance environment as it relates tologistics, security, and asset protection
Ability tooperate independently with a high degree of ownership and accountability
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills across internal and external partners
Analytical and structured approach to risk assessment and problem-solving
Fluent English (spoken and written); Hindi language proficiency preferred

It Will Be An Added Bonus If You Have

Experience in high-value or critical infrastructure supply chain security (e.g., data centers, AI hardware, electronics, technology hardware)
Background in Indian law enforcement, military (security-related roles), or corporate security
Familiarity with TAPA FSR, TAPA TSR, or equivalent supply chain security standards
Familiarity with supply chain security technologies (e.g., GPS tracking, geofencing, access control systems, CCTV, tamper-evident sealing)
Experience working within a global or regional organization with cross-border coordination requirements
Understanding of thelogistics and security landscape across key Indian cities and corridors, including major distribution hubs and inter-city freight routes

Operational Expectations

Dual-domain responsibility across warehouse and transportation security may require availability outside standard working hours for incident response across either domain
Operates within a global NGSCS environment requiring coordination across multiple time zones, including NGSCS teams in APAC, the EU, USA, Israel, and Taiwan
Travel across India is a core part of this role, given the country's geographic scale and the distribution of facilities andlogistics partners
Supported by the APAC Supply Chain Security Manager and NGSCS global leadership, with clear ownership of all supply chain security outcomes within India

Competitive compensation
Career growth and learning opportunities
Flexibility and ownership
Collaborative and innovative culture
Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

jobs.title: Senior Operations Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Spektrum supports apex purchasers (NATO, UN, EU and National Government and Defence) and their Tier 1 supplier ecosystem with a wide range of specialist services. We provide our clients with professional services, specialised aerospace and defence sales, delivery, and operational subject matter expertise. We are looking for personnel to join our team and support key client projects.
Who we are supporting

Allied Command Transformation (ACT)
is NATO’s leading agent for change: driving, facilitating, and advocating the continuous improvement of Alliance capabilities to maintain and enhance the military relevance and effectiveness of the Alliance. The main objectives of ACT are: providing appropriate support to NATO missions and operations; leading NATO military transformation; and improving relationships, interaction and practical cooperation with partners, nations and international organisations. ACT therefore leads Alliance concept development, capability development, training and lessons-learned initiatives and provides unfettered military support to policy development within NATO.
The program 

Capability Development & Management Support (CDMS)

DCOS Capability Development (CAPDEV)
acts as the Supreme Allied Commander Transformation's Director for guidance, direction and coordination of the activities and resources of the Capability Development Directorate.
The Requirements Division
will execute all tasks and activities needed to support requirements management for NATO capabilities
The Capability Requirements (CR)
Branch will develop the Capability Requirements Brief and recommended courses of action to resolve issues through the life cycle management of requirements using matrixed, cross-functional project-specific Requirements Management teams.
The Requirements Forward Branch (Mons)
is responsible for conducting requirements development and management representation and engagement-related functions in Europe.
The Capability Division
coordinates the development of capabilities from capability planning through acceptance and then disposal with management entities, NATO Headquarters staff and the NATO Governance Structure
The Capability Forward Branch (Mons)
coordinates with ACO, NCIA, NSPA, NATO HQ, territorial Host Nations, and NATO Centres of Excellence (COEs) to support the development of capabilities.
Strategic Plans and Policy (SPP)
supports Allied Command Transformation in formalizing military advice to shape future military strategy, political guidance, and other policy documents supporting NATO’s strategic objectives.
Role ID: ACT-CDMS-27-01-A-LC11

Role Background

The Operational Analysis Branch provides analysts to capability development programme teams to drive and support evidence-based decision making in requirements derivation and programmatic planning. In this SOW, “Operational Analysis” (predominantly military term) is used interchangeably with “Operations Research” (US term) and “Operational Research” (UK Term).
Course of Action (COA) analysis supports capability development programme teams to determine appropriate DOTMLPFI methods and capability architectures for meeting the military user’s operational requirements and defining programmatic structures.
Analysis of Alternatives (AoA) involves the comparative assessment of options in terms of costs, risks, schedules and operational effectiveness. The AoA tests the commercial marketplace and NATO’s ability to re-use capabilities that are in service in member Nations militaries. It establishes whether NATO should procure a managed service, adopt National capability solutions, acquire products from industry, or must develop bespoke solutions. For complex programmes, the AoA can inform programmatic structures by showing how value for money is most likely to be achieved.
NATO capability development decisions concern complex socio-technical systems, including computer information systems supporting NATO command and control, federated governance arrangements, capability integration activities and multinational delivery models. Analysts must be capable of combining quantitative and qualitative evidence and facilitating stakeholder engagement to support defensible decision-making. COA analysis and AoA typically involves engaging with the programme team to understand programmatic areas of uncertainty, designing and facilitating workshops to gather stakeholder views (including within the military NATO Command Structure, delivery Agencies and Centres of Excellence and / or the NATO Force Structure, gathering or generating (if appropriate) cost, risk schedule and effectiveness evidence, and comparative options assessment. This may include the development or elicitation of Measures of Performance (MoPs) and Measures of Effectiveness (MoEs); assessment of absolute and comparative risks; elicitation of schedule estimates; and review of cost estimates for appropriateness to support this assessment.
Operations Research methods can be applied at any stage of the capability development programme, including, but not limited to: decision science (e.g. multi-criteria decision analysis), optimization (e.g. linear programming), modelling & simulation, behavioural operations research, data science (e.g. advanced analytics and machine learning) and wargaming.
Roles Duties and Responsibilities

Contribute to Course of Action analysis using Operations Research and Analysis methods in support of Capability Development within ACT in order to mature NATO capability requirements and set programmatic direction.
Plan and conduct research to study and establish qualitative and quantitative assessments of operational effectiveness, undertake cost-effectiveness and risk-benefit studies and analyses.
Where necessary and appropriate, interact with NATO and National research entities and industries to establish the impact of alternatives on operational effectiveness.
Where necessary and appropriate, attend engagements or workshops with NATO, National organizations, and / or industry to ensure cost estimation activities are likely to provide outputs of appropriate quality to support analysis.
Support the creation of Requests for Information and surveys to NATO Nations, Non Governmental Organizations, and industry.
Analyse the potential impact of identified individual and aggregated risks, and propose possible risk management approaches.
Elicit, and / or review and assess schedule estimates, to ensure appropriate quality and supporting evidence for decisions being supported by analysis.
Review and assess cost estimates provided by others, to ensure appropriate quality and supporting evidence for decisions being supported by analysis.
Analyse and document comparative assessments of cost, risk, schedule and operational effectiveness to inform programmatic decision-making.
Produce decision briefs / presentations describing the underlying rationale / justification for analytical outcomes. If appropriate, brief decision-makers on the context, process and outcomes.
Produce written reports of analysis conducted as part of the Capability Programme plan evidence package, for review with the International Military Staff and International Staff in NATO Headquarters.
Produce summary briefs of lessons identified / lessons learned to support continuous improvement of NATO capability development and OA branch skills and competencies.
May be required to travel to meetings and conferences both within and outside NATO boundaries for up to 60 days per year.
Perform additional tasks as required by the COTR related to the LABOR category.

Essential Skills & Qualifications

Minimum two examples in the last 10 years (at least 3 years combined duration) in the field of military Operations Research / Operational Analysis / Data Science, supporting policy development, capability development or acquisition. With a relevant Bachelor’s degree (listed above), only 2 years in the last 5 must be in the fields / areas /listed above.
Experience designing, leading, and facilitating structured stakeholder engagements to elicit objectives, assumptions, measures, risks, preferences and expert judgement in support of defence capability decisions involving technical and non-technical stakeholders across multiple levels of seniority.
Experience, within last 5 years of determining Operations Research / Operational Analysis requirements, scoping problems for study, developing analysis plans, and delivering high quality outputs that influence senior decision makers.
Experience of developing data collection and analysis plans or assessment frameworks that include measures of effectiveness and measures of performance.
Experience in gathering evidence and scoring effectiveness through use of operations research and analysis methods to defence domain issues.
Experience identifying, eliciting, assessing, analysing and communicating uncertainty and risk associated with capability / acquisition, project, programme, or portfolio decisions.
Experience of producing or working with cost and schedule estimates, including estimating methodologies, methods and processes
Experience working in a strategic or operational military command or multinational organization.
Experience supporting project, programme, and / or portfolio decisions through analytical assessment in the past 10 years, within complex and dynamic programme environments.

Desirable Qualifications

Experience using AI to support OA.

Education or Relevant Professional Experience

A Bachelor’s degree in Operations Research, Mathematics, Computer Science, Physics, Engineering or equivalent quantitative degree. Alternatively, 5+ years of Operations Research/ Operational Analysis experience conducting and leading analytical studies in relevant military, strategic, political or international environment.

Language Proficiency

Business English

Norfolk, VA

Working Policy

Provide multi-site environmental compliance oversight for all cheese manufacturing and cheese packaging facilities in the network.
Provide site leadership guidance for the day-to-day environmental execution responsibility of local plants, including providing corporate governance, technical support, escalation, and assurance.
Lead and maintain oversight of environmental compliance programs across the organization, including wastewater, air emissions, stormwater, spill prevention, waste management, chemical reporting, permitting, recordkeeping, and regulatory submissions.
Maintain and guide the corporate environmental compliance governance model, ensuring clarity of roles and responsibilities across EHS, plant leadership, engineering, maintenance, operations, and external consultants.
