Join us in developing treatments, finding cures, and pioneering the path from lab to life while championing patients every step of the way. Learn more at https://www.jnj.com/innovative-medicine

We are searching for the best talent for a Director, European Health Data Space (EHDS) Programme Management
within our Clinical Data Transparency business. The position may be located Beerse, Belgium; Leiden, the Netherlands; High Wycombe/Maidenhead, UK; Allschwil, Switzerland; or Spring House / Titusville / Raritan, United States.
The position is Hybrid (3 days onsite weekly). Remote work options may be considered on a case-by-case basis and if approved by the company.

Please note that this role is available across multiple countries and may be posted under different requisition numbers to comply with local requirements. While you are welcome to apply to any or all of the postings, we recommend focusing on the specific country(s) that align with your preferred location(s):

United Kingdom- Requisition Number: R-100003

Belgium, Netherlands- Requisition Number: R-101024

United States - Requisition Number: R-101030

Switzerland - Requisition Number: R-101027

Remember, whether you apply to one or all of these requisition numbers, your applications will be considered as a single submission.

Position Summary

The Director provides strategic and operational leadership for Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine's European Health Data Space (EHDS) programme. Reporting to the Head of Clinical Data Standards & Transparency, IDAR, the role is accountable for defining and delivering the EHDS strategy, governance, operating model, and implementation roadmap, translating evolving regulatory requirements into sustainable business capabilities.

The Director leads a complex, cross-functional programme spanning Global Development, Legal, Privacy, Regulatory Affairs, Technology, Data Transparency, MedTech, and other business functions. Through matrix leadership, the role drives alignment, manages enterprise-wide dependencies, enables decision-making, and provides leadership with visibility of progress, risks, resources, and key decisions.

Dedicated to EHDS, the role may also support closely related Clinical Data Transparency priorities to ensure successful implementation and long-term adoption of EHDS capabilities.

You Will Be Responsible For

Sets the program management strategy and integrated delivery approach for EHDS, ensuring alignment between regulatory requirements, business priorities, technology enablement, and operational readiness.
Leads the integrated program plan, roadmap, milestones, outcomes, and success measures across Regulation Monitoring, Strategy Setting, Operating Model Design, Technology Enablement, Data Inventory and Cataloging, change management, and program governance.
Directs program execution across workstreams, establishes clear accountability for outcomes, and ensures delivery remains aligned to agreed scope, quality, compliance, resources, and priorities.
Establishes and oversees program governance, including decision rights, escalation pathways, integrated reporting, and the management of actions, risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies, and decisions.
Advises the EHDS Implementation Lead and senior governance bodies on program direction, delivery options, trade-offs, material risks, resource needs, and decisions required.
Navigates a complex stakeholder landscape, drives alignment on scope, requirements, priorities, and sequencing, and enables clear communication between leadership, workstream leads, business functions, and technology teams.
Anticipates and manages strategic and operational risks, dependencies, delivery constraints, and competing priorities; drives proactive mitigation and resolution and advances material matters through the appropriate governance pathways.
Directs resource and capacity planning across the program, including demand, allocation, external support, investment requirements, and the transition of capabilities into sustainable internal ownership.
Ensures technology-related activity is integrated with business requirements and operating processes, while maintaining clear accountability between business owners and technology delivery teams.
Defines and leads all aspects of the program change strategy, including impact assessment, engagement, communications, training, readiness, adoption, and transition to business-as-usual operations.
Oversees program performance, develops meaningful measures and insights, and uses them to identify corrective action, strengthen delivery rigor, and improve program efficiency.
Leads the development of executive materials and concise program reporting that provides visibility of delivery status, upcoming decisions, risks, interdependencies, and required leadership action.
Provides direction to external advisors, vendors, and communications partners; ensures deliverables, performance, and contractual expectations are aligned with program objectives.
Represents J&J on EHDS program delivery matters with relevant external bodies, industry groups, and partners, as required and in coordination with the appropriate subject matter experts.
Builds program management capability by establishing fit-for-purpose methods, tools, templates, and ways of working that can be sustained as EHDS requirements evolve.
If assigned direct reports, is accountable for hiring, development, coaching, performance management, and succession planning. Where the role operates as an individual contributor, provides functional direction, mentoring, and matrix leadership to program colleagues.

Are you ready to join our team? then please read further!

Education And Experience Requirements

Advanced degree in a scientific, technology, healthcare, or business discipline, or equivalent experience.
At least 10 years of relevant pharmaceutical, healthcare, technology, or scientific experience, including substantial leadership of large, complex, cross-functional programs!
Demonstrated ability to set program direction, establish governance, lead execution, and deliver outcomes across multiple functions in a global matrix environment.
Expert program and portfolio management capability, including integrated planning, risk and dependency management, resource planning, change, executive reporting, and decision governance.
Formal project or program management certification, such as PMP, PRINCE2, Agile, or SAFe, is preferred.
Working knowledge of the EU regulatory environment and data-related obligations; familiarity with EHDS, GDPR, clinical trial transparency, data governance, or regulated technology implementation is strongly preferred.
Ability to influence and negotiate with senior stakeholders, navigate ambiguity, and enable decisions where requirements and delivery pathways continue to evolve.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate regulatory and technical complexity into clear program choices, plans, and executive-level messages.
Demonstrated leadership in problem solving, critical thinking, prioritization, and decision making.
Experience leading people, senior individual contributors, vendors, or multidisciplinary teams.
Some domestic or international travel may be required.

Benefits

We offer a competitive salary and extensive benefits package. The health and well-being of our employees is a priority, we have a flexible working environment as we value work-life balance. We offer career development opportunities for those who want to grow and be part of our organisation. For additional general information on company benefits, please go to: https://www.careers.jnj.com/employee-benefits

People Leadership, Portfolio Management, Program Management

Preferred Skills

Advanced Analytics, Agile Methodology, Continuous Improvement, Database Management, Data Governance, Data Management, Data Privacy Standards, Data Savvy, Data Security, Data Stewardship, Emerging Technologies, Information Security Risk Management, Leadership, Performance Measurement, Strategic Thinking, Tactical Planning, Technical Credibility

Job Title: Deputy Program Manager

Job Category: Project and Program Management

Time Type: Full time

Minimum Clearance Required to Start: TS/SCI with Polygraph

Employee Type: Regular

Percentage of Travel Required: Up to 25%

Type of Travel: Local

* * *

The Opportunity

CACI is seeking an experienced Deputy Program Manager to lead the execution and growth of advanced national-security technology programs supporting Department of Defense and Intelligence Community customers.

Reporting to a Program/Portfolio Director, the Deputy Program Manager will be accountable for the cost, schedule, technical performance, financial results, and customer relationships associated with an assigned program or group of related projects. The portfolio includes research and development, product development, systems integration, production, fielding, sustainment, and mission support activities.

The successful candidate will be more than an administrative program manager. This leader will understand the customer’s mission, establish accountability across technical and business teams, maintain command of program financials, identify emerging risks early, and translate customer needs into executable and fundable work.

This position requires an active TS/SCI POLY clearance and is hybrid in either Sterling, VA or Jessup, MD.

Qualifications

Required:

Active TS/SCI POLY clearance.
Ten or more years of relevant professional experience, including at least five years leading programs, projects, or major technical workstreams for Department of Defense or Intelligence Community customers.
Demonstrated responsibility for a multimillion-dollar program, contract or task order.
Experience managing program financial performance, including revenue, margin, forecasts, estimates at completion, staffing, funding, and variance analysis.
Experience managing technical development, systems integration, production, sustainment, or mission-support programs.
Working knowledge of federal acquisition and contracting environments, including experience with one or more contract types such as CPFF, FFP, T&M, IDIQ, or task-order contracts.
Demonstrated ability to establish trusted relationships with government customers and communicate effectively with senior customer and company leadership.
Experience leading cross-functional teams containing technical, operational, contractual, and financial personnel.
Ability to organize ambiguous or evolving customer requirements into structured plans, assigned responsibilities, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, negotiation, written communication, and executive-briefing skills.
Demonstrated ability to identify deteriorating program conditions, develop corrective-action plans, and lead teams through recovery.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and program scheduling or collaboration tools.
Project Management Professional certification or ability to obtain within six months of hire.

Desired

Experience supporting classified research, development, engineering, production, or fielding programs.
Experience in one or more relevant mission areas, including RF systems, electronic warfare, SIGINT, communications, advanced electronics, cyber, sensing, or tactical mission systems.
Experience moving technology from prototype development through qualification, production, deployment, or operational sustainment.
Experience supporting Intelligence Community, USSOCOM, military-service, or other national-security customers.
Experience leading hardware, software, firmware, and systems-engineering activities within a common program structure.
Experience developing proposals, white papers, rough-order-of-magnitude estimates, bases of estimate, and contract-growth strategies.
Experience with Jira, Confluence, Microsoft Project, Deltek, or similar program-management and financial systems.
PMP, PgMP, Agile, SAFe, Lean Six Sigma, or related professional certification.

What You Can Expect

A culture of integrity.

At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation.

An environment of trust.

CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality.

A focus on continuous growth.

Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy.

new_jobs.title: Joint Space Protection (JSP) Program Manager (Science/Engineering Program Manager 4/5)
new_jobs.description:
What You Will Do

This position will be filled at either the Science/Engineering Program Manager 4 or 5 level, depending on the skills and experience of the selected candidate. Exceptional candidates may be considered for a higher-level position, and additional job responsibilities will be assigned if the candidate is hired at the higher level.

The Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) Global Security (GS) Directorate is seeking applicants for the Program Manager (PM) of the Joint Space Protection (JSP) Program. This position reports directly to the Program Directors for Intelligence and Emerging Threats (GS-IET) and National Security and Defense (GS-NSD).

The JSP provides space and ground solutions for Department of War (DOW) and Intelligence Community (IC) customer needs. These projects range from concept studies to data processing tools to spaceflight hardware. The JSP is currently executing ~$40M of projects in FY2026, with significant growth anticipated in FY2027. Note that DOW activities associated with the United States Nuclear Detonation Detection System (USNDS) are led by the Nuclear Nonproliferation and Security Program Office (GS-NNS).

Science/Engineering Program Manager 4 ($153,600-$266,500)

The PM leads the management, coordination, and development of JSP space activities and will serve as LANL's principal interface to the IC and DOW for all space related activities in coordination with the GS Program Directors and the GS Executive Advisor. The selected candidate will also advise Program Directors, Line Managers and internal investment boards (such as Laboratory-Directed Research and Development - LDRD) on the needs and opportunities of customer-funded space programs.

The JSP PM will coordinate with other LANL Program offices which conduct space activities as needed to set institutional priorities, resolve resource conflicts, and ensure coherent investments across the LANL space enterprise.

Science/Engineering Program Manager 5 ($184,200-$329,700)

In addition to what was outlined at the lower level, at this level the JSP PM will identify and coordinate strategic partnerships with other Federally Funded Research and Development Corporations (FFRDCs) and Commercial Industry to leverage LANL's unique capabilities for system development. This work will include collaboration with other LANL organizations, such as the Feynman Center for Innovation (FCI) to address legal aspects of collaboration.

What You Need

Minimum Job Requirements:

Technical Knowledge
: Demonstrated experience in space system design, production, and/or operations including a working familiarity with NASA and/or DOW Technical Readiness Level (TRL) assessment as it applies to space systems. The Program Manager is not expected to be an expert in all areas of space system design and operations but is expected to be conversant in critical areas and knowledgeable of integration and test.

Project Management:
Demonstrated ability to convert concepts and strategic objectives into executable projects with measurable outcomes. Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while balancing priorities and deadlines. Familiarity with coordinating interdisciplinary efforts and aligning project work with broader organizational goals. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail in both planning and execution.

Customer Relations and Stakeholder Engagement
: Ability to build effective working relationships with both internal and external stakeholders. Experience collaborating with leadership, subject matter experts, partner organizations, and/or public audiences. Ability to assess customer needs and translate them into achievable projects scopes and deliverables. Experience setting realistic expectations regarding project scope, timelines, resources, and deliverables.

Leadership
: Demonstrated peer-leadership ability to collaborate and strategize with colleagues to meet customer/project objectives while developing team members and meeting institutional goals.

Teamwork/Collaboration
: Demonstrated ability to foster a respectful, collaborative, and productive work environment. Ability to work constructively and professionally with colleagues across disciplines and backgrounds. Experience mentoring staff and supporting professional development. Willingness to share knowledge, provide constructive feedback, and support team success.

In addition to the duties outlined above, the Science/Engineering Program Manager 5 is expected to:

Technical Knowledge
: Demonstrated subject matter expertise in space system design, production, and/or operations. A SEPM 5 should be able to draw from past leadership experience of space system design, production, and/or operations.

Project Management:
Experience bringing projects through formal systems engineering reviews (e.g. SRR, PDR, CDR) including negotiating the content of these reviews with sponsors.

Customer Relations and Stakeholder Engagement:
Experience engaging with senior sponsors at the GS-15 level and above.

Education/Experience for Science/Engineering Program Manager 4:
Position requires a bachelor's degree in a science or engineering related field from an accredited institution and 12 years of directly related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience directly related to the occupation. At this level an advanced degree is typically expected. An advanced degree in a science or engineering field is preferred.

Education/Experience for Science/Engineering Program Manager 5:
Position requires a bachelor's degree in a science or engineering related field from an accredited institution and 15 years of directly related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience directly related to the occupation. At this level an advanced degree is typically expected. An advanced degree in a science or engineering field is preferred.

Desired Qualifications:

Expert knowledge of at least one of the following: space system hardware/software development, space ground system development, and/or space system operations.
Commercial or Government certification in program management, test, and/or systems engineering.
Functional understanding of Space Domain Awareness (SDA) and the roles of various US Government agencies in SDA.
Experience with the US DOW and/or IC space programs.
Active DOE Q clearance

Note to Applicants:

For full consideration, applicants must submit a comprehensive cover letter that addresses all the minimum requirements of the position.

Work Environment:

Work Location:
The work location for this position is onsite and located in Los Alamos, NM. All work locations are at the discretion of management.

Position commitment:
Regular appointment employees are required to serve a period of continuous service in their current position in order to be eligible to apply for posted jobs throughout the Laboratory. If an employee has not served the time required, they may only apply for Laboratory jobs with the documented approval of their Division Leader. The position commitment for this position is 1 year.

Note to Applicants:

Due to federal restrictions contained in the current National Defense Authorization Act, citizens of the People's Republic of China-including the special administrative regions of Hong Kong and Macau-as well as citizens of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea), and the Russian Federation, who are not Lawful Permanent Residents ("green card" holders) are prohibited from accessing facilities that support the mission, functions, and operations of national security laboratories and nuclear weapons production facilities, which includes Los Alamos National Laboratory. Where You Will Work

Located in beautiful northern New Mexico, Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) is a multidisciplinary research institution engaged in strategic science on behalf of national security. Our generous benefits package includes:

PPO or High Deductible medical insurance with the same large nationwide network
Dental and vision insurance
Free basic life and disability insurance
Paid childbirth and parental leave
Award-winning 401(k) (6% matching plus 3.5% annually)
Learning opportunities and tuition assistance
Flexible schedules and time off (PTO and holidays)
Onsite gyms and wellness programs
Extensive relocation packages (outside a 50 mile radius)

Additional Details

Directive 206.2
- Employment with Triad requires a favorable decision by NNSA indicating employee is suitable under NNSA Supplemental Directive 206.2. Please note that this requirement applies only to citizens of the United States. Foreign nationals are subject to a similar requirement under DOE Order 142.3A.

Clearance:
Q/SCI
(Position will be cleared to this level). Selected applicants will be subject to a background investigation conducted by or on behalf of the Federal Government, and must meet eligibility requirements* for access to classified matter. This position requires a Q clearance. and obtaining such clearance requires US Citizenship except in extremely rare circumstances. Dependent upon the position, additional authorization to access classified information may be required, which may or may not be available to dual citizens. Receipt of a Q clearance and additional access authorization ultimately is a decision of the Federal Government and not of Triad.

Eligibility requirements: To obtain a clearance, an individual must be at least 18 years of age; U.S. citizenship is required except in very limited circumstances. See DOE Order 472.2 for additional information.

New-Employment Drug Test:
The Laboratory requires successful applicants to complete a new-employment drug test and maintains a substance abuse policy that includes random drug testing. Although New Mexico and other states have legalized the use of marijuana, use and possession of marijuana remain illegal under federal law. A positive drug test for marijuana will result in termination of employment, even if the use was pre-offer.

Regular position
: Term status Laboratory employees applying for regular-status positions are converted to regular status.

Internal Applicants:
Regular appointment employees who have served the required period of continuous service in their current position are eligible to apply for posted jobs throughout the Laboratory. If an employee has not served the required period of continuous service, they may only apply for Laboratory jobs with the documented approval of their Division Leader. Please refer to Policy P701 for applicant eligibility requirements.

Incentive Compensation Program:
Position is eligible to participate in the Triad Incentive Compensation Program. You must be in an eligible position for a minimum of 3 months, before July 1st and remain in an eligible position as of the end of the fiscal year, September 30th. The annual distribution is prorated based on the number of months in the eligible position.

Equal Opportunity:
Los Alamos National Laboratory is an equal opportunity employer. All employment practices are based on qualification and merit, without regard to protected categories such as race, color, national origin, ancestry, religion, age, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status or spousal affiliation, physical or mental disability, medical conditions, pregnancy, status as a protected veteran, genetic information, or citizenship within the limits imposed by federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The Laboratory is also committed to making our workplace accessible to individuals with disabilities and will provide reasonable accommodations, upon request, for individuals to participate in the application and hiring process. To request such an accommodation, please send an email to applyhelp@lanl.gov or call (505)-664-6947.

new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager (Hybrid)
new_jobs.description:
About Rewards Network

For 41 years, Rewards Network has been helping restaurants grow revenue, increase traffic, and boost customer engagement through innovative financial, marketing services, and premier dining rewards programs. By offering unique card-linked offers, we introduce diners to fantastic restaurant experiences, leveraging advanced technology and data analytics to deliver value to restaurants, diners, and our strategic partners' loyalty programs.

Our Culture

At Rewards Network, you'll be part of a driven and diverse team that excels in collaboration, issue resolution, and taking ownership of both personal growth and the company's success. We take pride in partnering with the world's most powerful loyalty programs to drive full-price paying customers to local restaurants through marketing services and flexible funding options. Our engaging and rewarding environment is designed to help you gain your full potential.

Job Overview

The Senior Technical Program Manager at Rewards Network owns the planning, governance, and delivery of the company's most complex, strategic programs — including large-scale product transformations on our consumer- and restaurant-facing sides of the business, major product modernization initiatives (from discovery through launch), large-scale partner and restaurant onboarding programs, new strategic partner and payments integrations, and core payments infrastructure upgrades and migrations. Each of these spans multiple concurrent workstreams across Product, Engineering, Data, Partner Management, Marketing, and Operations. This role owns the end-to-end timeline, success, and delivery health of that program portfolio — from Conception through launch — establishing the operating rhythm and managing cross-program dependencies, risk, and stakeholder communication so Rewards Network's highest-priority initiatives land on time, meet a standard of greatness, and align with business objectives.

This is an embedded owner into the cross-functional team: someone senior enough to operate without handholding, deep enough in the details of the work to know why each program matters (not just its next milestone), and comfortable reporting credibly in both directions — upward (to executives and senior leaders) with clean, balanced, actionable updates, and outward (to Partners, Ops, Marketing, and Engineering) to ensure alignment. This role reports directly to the Senior Director of Product and is an experienced individual contributor role for someone who thrives at the intersection of rigorous program governance and cross-functional influence at the executive level.

This is a hybrid position that requires in office presence 3 days a week (Tuesday-Thursday) in Chicago.

What you’ll bring to the table: (Responsibilities)

Own end-to-end program management for Rewards Network's most complex, cross-functional strategic initiatives — spanning platform transformations, product modernization efforts, large-scale partner and merchant onboarding, new partner and payments integrations, and core payments infrastructure upgrades — often managing several concurrently.
Define and maintain program plans, timelines, milestones, and cross-program dependency maps; drive accountability against committed dates and quality bars.
Proactively identify, track, and mitigate risks and issues; escalate appropriately and recommend trade-offs when scope, schedule, or resources require rebalancing.
Work with Product leadership to ensure the right work is sequenced against available resources. Establish and run the governance operating model — steering committees, working-team cadences, and review rhythms — to keep each program's health visible without active leadership involvement.
Own program-level reporting and status communication to executives, senior leadership, and key stakeholders; translate complex delivery details across multiple concurrent programs into simple, clear, decision-ready summaries.
Manage cross-program dependencies with internal partners and external integrations (e.g., loyalty program partners); ensure alignment on requirements, timelines, and acceptance criteria across every program in the portfolio.
Own the cross-functional execution of product launches and go-to-market plans: coordinate readiness, dependencies, timing, and stakeholder alignment across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Legal, Finance, and Partner Management. Partner closely with Marketing on positioning and messaging, but owns the plan, the timeline, and an on-time, successful delivery.
Serve as the primary point of contact and connective tissue for cross-functional programs — this includes applying pressure (or escalation) to other leaders as needed to keep programs on-track.
Continuously improve program management practices, tools, templates, and governance processes, including eliciting feedback on how we can continue to improve them.
Leverage AI tools and workflows to increase program management velocity and quality — accelerating status synthesis, risk analysis, and plan generation — and model AI-native practices for the broader cross-functional team.
Champion a culture of clear ownership, transparent communication, and continuous improvement across the organization.

Do you have the right mix of ingredients: (Requirements)

Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
7-10 years of technical program or project management experience delivering software/technology initiatives in a SaaS, B2B, B2C, or B2B2C environment, including experience managing a portfolio of related, concurrent programs.
Demonstrated experience leading a portfolio of multiple concurrent, related programs from inception to launch, with enough technical fluency to engage credibly with Engineering on architecture, sequencing, and risk.
Experience working with Agile delivery teams (Scrum, Kanban, or hybrid).
Experience presenting program-level status to executives and senior-leaders.
Demonstrated ability to ramp quickly into ambiguous, in-flight programs and operate independently within days or weeks, not months.
Strong program and project management fundamentals: scope definition, scheduling, cross-program dependency management, identifying risks, risk management, and change control.
Excellent ability to translate ambiguous business goals into structured, actionable plans with clear milestones and accountability.
Proven experience leading cross-functional programs (engineering, design, product, marketing, partner management, operations) without direct authority.
Operates as an embedded owner, not a meeting scheduler or status relay — brings a point of view on risk and sequencing rather than simply passing along what others report.
Comfortable partnering with Product Marketing and Marketing on go-to-market execution — translating an agreed positioning and messaging strategy into a coordinated, cross-functional launch plan, timeline, and readiness checklist.
Proficiency with program and project management and collaboration tools: JIRA, Confluence, Asana, Miro; comfort with reporting tools and dashboards (e.g., advanced JIRA, Tableau, or similar). Experience designing and running a program governance model — steering committees, working-team cadences, and demo/review rhythms — that scales with a program's complexity.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to use data to inform planning, identify bottlenecks, and measure delivery health.
World-class written and verbal communication skills; ability to tailor messaging from individual contributors up to executive leadership.
Calm under pressure with strong stakeholder management, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills.
AI-native and proficient with modern AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Glean, Claude) to accelerate day-to-day program management — drafting plans and status updates, synthesizing data across systems, and surfacing risks faster — with a mindset of continuously adopting new AI-enabled workflows as they emerge.
Ability to manage multiple, complex, competing priorities in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment. 

Education, Certifications and Experience: Preferred

PMP, PgMP, CSM, PMI-ACP or equivalent program/project management certification.
Experience in FinTech, MarTech, restaurant, dining, hospitality, or loyalty/rewards industries.
Experience coordinating with external partners (e.g., loyalty programs, integration partners, vendors) on joint roadmaps and delivery commitments.
Experience coordinating product launches or go-to-market execution in partnership with Product Marketing or Marketing teams.
Experience managing data, analytics, or AI/ML-driven product initiatives.

What You’ll Love About Us

Comprehensive benefits package, which includes:

This is a full-time, exempt position. The base salary range for this role in Chicago is $140,000–$160,000 annually, depending on candidate's experience, as well as skills, and other factors. This role is also eligible for an annual bonus target of 15%, bringing total target compensation to $161,000–$184,000.

new_jobs.description:
About Us:
At Booking.com, data drives our decisions. Technology is at our core. And innovation is everywhere. But our company is more than datasets, lines of code or A/B tests. We’re the thrill of the first night in a new place. The excitement of the next morning. The friends you encounter. The journeys you take. The sights you see. And the memories you make. Through our products, partners and people, we make it easier for everyone to experience the world.

About the team:
Booking.com IT Services size and technical complexity require specialists who can drive cross-organisational initiatives with significant technology dependencies. As a Technical Program Manager, you will lead delivery from problem framing through implementation and measurable outcome. You will work directly with engineering, product and operational stakeholders to establish scope, ownership, realistic plans, delivery rhythms and decision-making. You will bring an independent view of progress, surface risk early and help teams make practical trade-offs without adding unnecessary process.

This is an individual-contributor role. It does not include people management. The role may support global services and stakeholders, but its organisational delivery scope is calibrated to TPM rather than Senior TPM.

About the role:
You will independently lead the delivery of technically complex, cross-team initiatives that solve business and internal-customer problems. Working across several engineering and product teams, typically within one track or product group, you will translate an end-to-end technical solution into a realistic program structure, align priorities and ownership, and deliver incremental, measurable value for Booking.com employees and internal customers.

Who you work with

Internal stakeholders

You will work continuously with engineering, product, operations, security, privacy and business teams across Booking.com and relevant Booking Holdings functions. The role requires cooperation, persuasion and clear information-sharing to align priorities and deliver outcomes.

External stakeholders

You may work frequently with technology and service vendors, using clear requirements, delivery plans, risk ownership and performance expectations to support program outcomes.

Role accountability

This is an individual-contributor role with no direct people-management or P&L responsibility. Programs may support globally distributed teams and services, while the organisational delivery scope remains aligned with a TPM role: normally several teams within a track or product group. Decisions and outcomes typically influence the short-to-mid-term delivery horizon.

Perhaps in the "what you bring" mentioning expertise of different delivery methodologies (such as Agile and Lean)?

Key Job Responsibilities And Duties

Lead small-to-medium, technically complex programs and cross-team initiatives with meaningful business or internal-customer impact, normally spanning several teams within a track or product group.
Translate business and internal-customer problems, technical designs and non-functional requirements into a clear delivery structure, milestones and iterative value slices.
Create and maintain realistic, outcome-based plans using relevant delivery and operational metrics.
Clarify decision rights, ownership and accountability across workstreams; make dependencies and the critical path visible.
Identify and manage technical and delivery risks, issues and changes; define mitigation plans (after discussing options with the right owners)
Build alignment across engineering, product, security, privacy, operations and business stakeholders, influencing without formal authority.
Communicate concise program updates and decisions at the right level of detail, including to Director-level stakeholders.
Establish fit-for-purpose governance and delivery practices that work across teams with different ways of working.
Use retrospectives, delivery data and feedback to improve predictability, quality and team collaboration.
Contribute practical learning and reusable delivery practices to the TPM craft community.
Define and maintain program documentation, ensure functional and non-functional requirements are captured, and partner with engineering teams so supporting technical documentation is produced and maintained.
Drive the planning, documentation and communication of strategic programs with leaders across Booking.com and, where relevant, Booking Holdings.

What success looks like

Teams understand the outcome, their ownership and how their work connects to the end-to-end solution.
Plans are credible, continuously updated and focused on incremental value rather than activity alone.
Risks, dependencies and priority conflicts are visible early and have clear owners and decisions.
Stakeholders receive concise, evidence-based information and can make timely trade-offs.
Programs deliver measurable business, employee, reliability, security, cost or operational outcomes.
Delivery practices become simpler and more effective without creating unnecessary governance.

Role Qualifications And Requirements

5+ years of relevant experience in product, project, program or technical program management, working directly with engineering or software-development teams to build, implement or launch technical solutions.
Evidence of personally leading an end-to-end technical program lifecycle: discovery, scope, planning, execution, release or implementation, outcome measurement and learning.
Technical fluency sufficient to understand and explain system components, interfaces, data flows, functional and non-functional requirements, testing or release approaches, failure modes and trade-offs.
Strong delivery-management capability, including iterative planning, sequencing, dependency management, critical-path awareness, risk and issue management, and useful progress metrics.
Ability to align stakeholders and influence decisions without authority, including when teams have competing priorities.
Clear written, verbal and visual communication; able to adapt detail and framing for engineers, managers and Directors.
A data-informed, customer-oriented and pragmatic approach to navigating ambiguity, solving problems and making decisions.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong business awareness and technical vision.
Curiosity and ability to understand architectural and technical aspects of programs and their long-term consequences.
Expertise of different delivery methodologies (such as Agile and Lean)

Preferred Context

Cloud infrastructure, SaaS business applications or DevOps practices.
Identity and access management, including platforms such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or Ping Identity; networking, remote access or internal-platform services.
Programs serving internal customers, including work with vendors or distributed teams.
Programming or engineering background; business-continuity, regulatory or compliance exposure.
Jira, Jira Align or comparable planning and delivery tooling.

AI affinity and mindset

Show curiosity and practical understanding of AI tools and how they can improve work, not just generic enthusiasm.
Demonstrate safe AI habits: awareness of hallucinations, privacy, data handling, corporate guardrails, and the need to validate outputs.

new_jobs.description:
About The Role

Riverbend Energetics is seeking an experienced Program Manager II to lead and execute complex defense programs involving energetic components, electric/stab detonators, and CAD/PAD systems for U.S. defense customers. In this role, you will serve as the primary customer interface and internal program champion, driving program performance across cost, schedule, and technical objectives. This is a high-visibility opportunity to shape mission-critical programs that directly support U.S. national defense.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned defense program customers, managing relationships with program offices, prime contractors, and government agencies throughout the program lifecycle
Lead Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and finance to execute programs on time and within budget
Develop, maintain, and report on program plans, schedules, budgets, and Earned Value Management (EVM) metrics to internal leadership and external customers
Identify, assess, and actively mitigate program risks and opportunities, maintaining formal risk registers and presenting status at program and executive reviews
Manage Contract Data Requirements Lists (CDRLs) and ensure timely, compliant delivery of all contractual deliverables
Support proposal development activities including work breakdown structure (WBS) development, basis-of-estimate (BOE) generation, and schedule development for new business pursuits
Partner with business development and capture teams to support customer calls, program reviews, and organic growth opportunities within existing program portfolios

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or a related technical or management discipline
Minimum 5 years of program management experience in the defense industry, including direct ownership of cost, schedule, and technical performance
Demonstrated experience managing U.S. government contracts in a FAR/DFARS environment, including firm-fixed-price (FFP) and cost-type contract vehicles
Proficiency with program scheduling tools (e.g., Microsoft Project) and program performance reporting
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to present program status to senior leadership and government customers
U.S. citizenship required; must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Defense security clearance
Ability to work on-site at Riverbend Energetics facilities in compliance with applicable explosive safety regulations and site security requirements

Preferred Qualifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or Defense Acquisition University (DAU) program management credentials
Experience managing programs involving energetic materials, ordnance, pyrotechnics, or other hazardous or regulated defense hardware
Familiarity with DODIC/NSN systems, MIL-spec requirements, and defense ordnance qualification processes (e.g., HERO, ESD, drop/shock testing)
Active DoD Secret or Top Secret security clearance
Experience with AS9100 or equivalent quality management systems in a defense manufacturing environment
Prior military service or direct experience working within a government program office

What We Offer

Competitive salary and benefits package
The opportunity to lead programs that directly support U.S. warfighter readiness and national security at a specialized, innovative defense manufacturer
A collaborative, mission-driven culture where program managers have meaningful authority and visibility across a 150-person organization
Professional development support including training, certification assistance, and pathways to senior program leadership roles

Key Requirements

Defense Acquisition & Contracting Fluency: Riverbend operates exclusively in the U.S. defense market under FAR/DFARS regulations with FFP and cost-type contracts. A PM who truly understands the government acquisition lifecycle — not just nominally — will move faster, make fewer compliance errors, and build credibility with government program offices. At a 150-person company, there is no large contracts department to backstop a PM who lacks this knowledge.
Cross-Functional Authority Without Direct Control: The PM leads Integrated Product Teams spanning engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and finance — none of whom report directly to them. At a 150-person company, formal authority is limited and influence is everything. A PM who relies on org-chart power will stall programs; one who builds trust and creates accountability across functions will consistently deliver.
Hazardous / Regulated Hardware Program Experience: Energetic components, detonators, and CAD/PAD systems carry unique regulatory, safety, and qualification burdens — HERO, ESD, MIL-spec compliance, explosive safety site plans — that do not exist in standard defense hardware programs. A PM unfamiliar with this environment will underestimate risk, misschedule qualification activities, and create safety or compliance exposure. This is the single biggest differentiator from a generic defense PM.
Customer Relationship Management Under Pressure: The PM is the primary face to government program offices and prime contractors. Defense customers have long memories, and relationships built or damaged at the program level directly affect re-compete positioning and organic growth. At a small, specialized company like Riverbend, losing a key customer relationship is a material business risk — there is no account team to absorb the damage.
Rigorous Risk & Schedule Discipline: Defense energetics programs involve long-lead materials, tightly regulated test sequences, and low-volume, high-consequence deliverables where a single schedule slip can affect warfighter readiness. A PM at Riverbend must maintain formal, credible risk registers and schedules — not as reporting theater, but as actual management tools. In a small company without deep program management infrastructure, the PM must personally enforce this discipline.

About Riverbend Energetics

Riverbend Energetics is a defense and industrial manufacturer based in Alton, IL. We develop and produce energetic materials and specialty munitions for U.S. defense and allied customers. Our mission-critical work demands precision, safety, and a commitment to excellence.

new_jobs.title: Marketing Business Operations Manager
new_jobs.description:
Who are we?

At UpGuard, we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

Where does this role fit in?

We are seeking a Marketing Business Operations Manager to own the marketing budget process end-to-end and act as the operational backbone of the marketing team.

This role goes beyond coordination and support, you'll independently design and drive process and systems improvements, own the team's work management platform, and lead change management for new ways of working across marketing.

It's best suited to someone who already operates with real ownership and is ready to bring that judgment to a fast-moving marketing organisation.

What will you do?

Process & Systems Support

Own identification of friction points in how work moves between Marketing teams (shared services and squads), and lead the design and rollout of improvements
Own admin-level configuration and governance of the team's work management platform (Asana), including templates, custom fields, rules, and work structure standards
Lead evaluation and implementation of automation and no-code tooling, including AI tools, to scale the team's capacity
Lead change management for new processes and tools across the marketing team, including initiatives driven by leadership, and support the team through transitions

Budget Ownership & Financial Planning

Own the marketing budget process end-to-end, leading annual planning in partnership with department heads across the marketing organization
Lead the monthly forecasting cycle, reconcile actuals against budget, and proactively surface risks and opportunities to leadership
Build and maintain budget models and dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into spend
Partner with Finance on budget governance, ensuring documentation and reporting standards are met
Oversee vendor invoicing and purchase order processes, resolving escalations as needed

Events & Logistics

Oversee the planning and execution of internal marketing events, including venue and vendor strategy
Oversee travel arrangements and event logistics for the marketing team, resolving complex or escalated issues
Own meeting scheduling and calendar strategy for marketing leadership, including recurring cadences
Facilitate executive meetings, ensuring effective structure, capture decisions and drive follow-through, and follow-through on action items
Own the strategy and vendor relationships for the company's online swag store, including budget and forecasting, and own the internal request process end-to-end.

Tools, Content & Reporting

Own and continuously evolve the marketing team's Notion workspace and team handbooks
Own the marketing team's Asana project, setting best practices for tasks, timelines, and status reporting
Own marketing goal tracking within Asana, partnering with leadership to ensure strategic alignment
Develop and refine presentation materials for quarterly global marketing meetings, incorporating strategic narrative
Own agenda-setting and preparation for key marketing meetings, partnering directly with leadership

What will you bring?

3+ years of experience designing and improving workflows and processes across teams, ideally within a shared-services or squad-based structure
Demonstrated, admin-level experience managing a work management platform (Asana, Monday, or similar)
Strong systems thinking, able to see an operating model holistically, not just optimize individual tools
Proven experience with automation or no-code tooling, including AI tools
Demonstrated change management or facilitation experience, with a track record of driving adoption of new ways of working
Demonstrated experience owning a budget process end-to-end, not just tracking spend
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work confidently with senior stakeholders

What will give you an edge?

Experience specifically within a marketing function, versus a generalist ops/PM background
Data and reporting skills, e.g. building capacity models to identify trends and scaling opportunities
Experience partnering with or managing external vendors and contractors
Experience mentoring or guiding junior team members

What's in it for you?

Monthly Lifestyle subsidy: Use this for financial, physical, and mental well-being
WFH set-up allowance: To ensure you have the right environment to work in, we will help you get set up within your first 3 months at UpGuard
$1500 USD annual Learning & Development allowance: To support your career development, all team members will be able to expense development opportunities against this allowance
Annual leave: PTO plus two additional UpGuardian leave days to give you time to recharge your batteries.
18 weeks paid Parental Leave: Irrespective of parenting role
Personal Leave Allowance: This includes sick & carer’s leave
Fully remote working environment: While we have physical offices in Sydney & Hobart, we do not mandate compulsory attendance
Top-spec hardware: All team members will be provided with top-spec laptops for their role
Generative AI subsidy: UpGuard provides paid subscriptions for all team members to access generative AI tools to support their work

UpGuard is a Certified Great Place to Work® in the US, Australia, UK and India, establishing its position as a leading global technology employer. 99% of team members agree that UpGuard is a great place to work! Apply now to find out why!

As an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer, qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.

new_jobs.description:
Cammach are working with an established and growing engineering consultancy based in Aberdeen who are looking to appoint a Project Manager on a permanent (staff) basis. This is an exciting opportunity to join the business at an important stage of its growth.

ROLE

The successful candidate will effectively be responsible for establishing and developing a new project delivery function/division within the business, putting the structure, processes and controls in place to manage projects from the point of sale through to successful delivery.

Responsibilities

Taking ownership of projects/orders following handover from Sales.
Acting as the principal interface between the client and the company’s internal teams throughout project execution.
Establishing a clear project management process covering the journey from order through to delivery.
Introducing appropriate procedures, documentation, reporting and project controls.
Coordinating activities across engineering, manufacturing, suppliers, testing and other areas involved in delivery.
Managing priorities, timescales and client expectations.
Identifying potential issues or delays early and driving actions through to resolution.
Ensuring everyone involved understands responsibilities, deadlines and deliverables.
Supporting the introduction and delivery of new products, where projects may not necessarily follow an established template or process.
Helping create a scalable project delivery structure that can support the company as the business and its product portfolio continue to develop.

Requirements

Candidates may come from a Project Engineer, Senior Project Engineer, Lead Engineer, or technically focused Project Manager background, provided they have the confidence, leadership, and organisational ability to take ownership of the function.
Strong well intervention experience would be particularly valuable, enabling the successful candidate to understand the practical application of the company’s products and engage credibly in technical discussions with both customers and the internal engineering team.
Strong attention to detail: Naturally identifies missing information, outstanding actions and potential project issues, taking proactive steps to address them rather than waiting for problems to be highlighted.
Process-driven and pragmatic: Able to introduce clear, sensible processes that improve project delivery, while avoiding unnecessary bureaucracy or process for its own sake.
Strong sense of ownership: Takes responsibility for projects from initial handover through to final delivery, ensuring issues are followed through to resolution rather than assuming someone else will pick them up.
Strong customer communication: Comfortable acting as a key interface between the company and the customer throughout project execution, managing expectations and communicating technical and project information clearly and professionally.
Ability to coordinate across teams: Able to influence and coordinate people across different functions, even where there is no direct line-management responsibility. Confident setting expectations, driving actions and keeping teams aligned towards delivery.
Comfortable with change and growth: Adaptable and motivated by the opportunity to help shape and develop the way the company manages projects. This is not a role where you will inherit a fully mature project management system; you will have the opportunity to build and improve processes as the business grows.

A Note on Profile Match:
To be successful in this role, you’ll need deep experience in international TV viewership trends and media audience insights. While we love working with technical data teams, please note that this is a commercial viewer insights role and is not a fit for Data Scientists or Data Engineers.

The role

As part of the Global Data and Insights team at ITV Studios, one of our core currencies is Global TV audience viewing data
. Your mission is to turn complex global TV ratings into powerful, commercially driven narratives that maximise revenue across Global Distribution Sales (scripted, unscripted, and formats), Branded Partnerships (Studio 55), and Content & Production.

First and foremost, you are an expert in UK and international TV ratings and audience measurement
. Key international markets you’ll be familiar with include the US, Canada, France, Germany, Spain, Italy, Benelux, Nordics and Australia. As the Lead Data Analyst, you will lead the insights strategy
for the Global Viewing team. You understand how to blend traditional TV ratings (like BARB and Nielsen) with market intelligence (Ampere, K7, NoTa) and streaming data to understand why content travels, contextualise performance, and fuel high-value global TV sales pitches.

The ideal candidate will seamlessly bridge the gap between people management, strategic storytelling, and technical proficiency, inspiring a team of analysts while effectively communicating complex findings to stakeholders at all levels.

In this role, you will act as the crucial commercial and analytical bridge setting the requirements for our Studio’s technology team to build data products which centralise and join a variety of 3rd party data sources together to make analysis and self-serve tooling easier . You will translate complex media measurement logic into clear tech requirements, ensuring the testing and data quality are robust so our data estate supports automated, self-serve insights that seamlessly integrate streaming metrics alongside linear results.

You will act as the primary strategic partner for three critical internal business arms:

Global Sales:
Crafting compelling, data-driven "sales stories" to maximise distribution revenue.
Global Content
: Delivering objective performance tracking to inform crucial commissioning and renewal decisions.
Production Labels
: Providing trends and viewing analysis to support creative development across our 60+ labels.

Main Responsibilities

Commercial Sales Storytelling:
Work hand-in-hand with the propositions manager to translate raw viewing metrics and digital viewing trends into persuasive sales angles. You will find the data nuggets that prove a show’s value to international buyers—whether that's retention metrics, streaming performance, or demographic advertising strengths.
Creative & Renewal Benchmarking:
Use historical TV ratings and streaming data to provide realistic success benchmarks for new commissions, explaining exactly why a show succeeded or failed in specific territories.
Label Partnership
: Act as the trusted data partner to our production labels, giving them the objective tracking they need to refine their shows, combined with "sales-style" highlights to celebrate wins.
Team Leadership
: Manage and mentor a small, agile team of analysts, keeping them focused on advanced, automated analysis over manual, repetitive reporting.
Audience Measurement Strategy (In Conjunction with Tech)
: set the high-level requirement for data joins which speed up and automate analysis which is commercially and strategically valuable
Data Extraction & API Querying
: Utilise SQL to actively query and extract performance data directly from BARB APIs and other international viewing databases. While engineers build the pipeline architecture, you will dive into the data to solve fast-turnaround commercial questions and prototype new data models or reporting automations.
Data Pipelines & Automation Requirements
: Partner with external engineering teams to design and automate data workflows across the wider digital ecosystem. You will help define the rules that seamlessly connect our internal content catalogue with external ratings and streaming data,

Skills You'll Need (Minimum Criteria)

Expert TV Ratings & Streaming Knowledge
: Deep, hands-on expertise with BARB and international viewing panel datasets (e.g., Nielsen, AGF, Mediametrie, Oztam). You must intimately understand how digital streaming data complements linear metrics (ratings, share), SVOD/BVOD/AVOD tracking, and the complexities of harmonising them.
Wider Digital Ecosystem Awareness:
A comprehensive understanding of the evolving digital video landscape and modern cross-media audience measurement frameworks.
Master Storyteller & Commercial Partner
: Proven experience working directly alongside Commercial or Sales teams. You don't just report numbers; you know how to weave data into creative "sales stories," validate pitch angles, and directly support high-value buyer negotiations.
Strategic Media Analytics Leadership
: Extensive background working specifically within a media data analytics or audience research function.
Advanced SQL for Data Retrieval:
Strong proficiency in SQL is mandatory. You must be comfortable using SQL to extract, manipulate, and blend data directly from APIs (such as the BARB API) and cloud warehouses. Python an added bonus
Technical Cross-Functional Collaboration
: Proven experience working in conjunction with Data and technology teams. You have a track record of translating business and audience data needs into technical requirements for pipelines, data warehousing, or BI solutions.
Pragmatic Problem Solving
: A proactive approach to audience data limitations, with the ability to develop clever proxy metrics when official panel data is missing or restricted.
Data Visualisation:
Solid experience working with BI platforms (Looker, Tableau, or PowerBI) to turn raw numbers into clean, narrative-driven visual tools for non-technical stakeholders.

About BorrowPit.com

BorrowPit.com is a national marketplace and brokerage for dirt, fill, and aggregate. We connect contractors, developers, and project owners with material sources and disposal solutions across Texas and beyond. 
The Opportunity

This is not a traditional sales role. The best people in this role win because they know more about what is happening in their market than anyone else. If that is how you already think about your work, reach out.
We are building our presence in one of the most active construction markets in the country. Industrial projects, data centers, land development, and infrastructure work are all moving significant amounts of dirt and the demand is not slowing down.
We are building something in a market that still runs on phone calls and handshakes. The people who win here combine those relationships with real intelligence about what is happening on the ground. That combination is what BorrowPit.com is built around.
What You Will Do

Research and identify active and upcoming construction projects using permit data, project databases, and construction intelligence platforms — getting to opportunities before they hit the open market
Evaluate projects for import and export material opportunities and locate key contacts including owners, GCs, subcontractors, and land teams
Build and maintain a living database of active projects, contacts, material needs, and market pricing within your territory
Source and broker dirt, fill, and aggregate import and export opportunities on active projects
Coordinate trucking and logistics on active deals including sourcing carriers, obtaining rates, and managing delivery schedules
Build and manage relationships with GCs, earthwork subs, developers, and land teams
Use and actively contribute to BorrowPit.com's internal data intelligence tool, adding project data, supplier information, and market pricing that makes the platform smarter every day
Log all activity, opportunities, and communications in HubSpot CRM daily and keep project pages complete and up to date
Represent BorrowPit.com as the go-to earthwork sourcing partner in your market

What You Bring

5-10 years of experience in construction, materials, earthwork, logistics, or land development
Existing relationships with contractors, developers, or project teams in your market
Naturally curious — you dig into a project to understand the full scope before making contact
Comfortable working with project databases, permit data, and construction intelligence platforms to find opportunities others miss
Thinks like a researcher and acts like a dealmaker, using data and intelligence to prioritize who to call and why before picking up the phone
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, managing a complex pipeline without being reminded

new_jobs.title: Senior Lead Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

The Data Science & Analytics organization at Realtor.com is looking for a Senior Data Analyst to join our team as a strategic partner supporting Lead Intelligence & Revenue Optimization. This role will provide strategic insights and data driven guidance to support the creation of a unified engine that strategically supports the full lifecycle of a lead—optimizing lead generation and inventory allocation to maximize organizational yield and client satisfaction.

As a Senior Data Analyst, you will not just report data; you will be a key analytical engine driving our revenue management strategy. You will work at the intersection of supply quality and demand yield, using data to drive precise decisioning for geo-targeted marketing and smart inventory management.

Top Reasons To Apply

High-Impact Marketplace Optimization: You will directly influence revenue routing and inventory yield strategies across a massive, national two-sided marketplace.
Full Ownership of Next-Gen Data Layers: Transition V1 builds from external vendors into internal hands, taking full ownership of our predictive close models and Lead-To-Transact pipeline.
Complex Data Problem Solving: Uncover non-obvious revenue streams, such as identifying low-priority land-listing leads that actually convert into high-value single-family home transactions.
Direct Stakeholder & Executive Visibility: Partner directly with Product, Tech, Pricing, and Engineering teams to transform complex statistical insights into executive dashboards and automated allocation rules.

What You’ll Do

Lead Intelligence Strategy & Support: Act as the primary analytical partner for the Lead Intelligence initiative, helping to define and align lead inventory allocation and optimization across all geographies.
Advanced Forecasting & Modeling: Evolve and improve sophisticated forecasting models for lead delivery and sales pipeline. You will perform scenario analysis to maximize outcomes while optimizing the consumer and client experience.
Inventory & Yield Optimization: Conduct deep-dive analyses to identify and prioritize high-value leads by geography and intent signal. Use these insights to recommend rules-based allocation strategies that optimize yield.
Impact Simulation: Simulate and report on the knock-on effects of changes to product eligibility and allocation rules across various business units.
KPI Development & Monitoring: Track and forecast lead delivery for operational planning, building new KPIs to measure the success of lead outcomes and revenue optimization.
Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with Product, Tech, Pricing, and Client Engineering teams to ensure the standardized implementation of rules across the RDC ecosystem. What You’ll Bring
Education & Experience: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Analytics, Math, Economics, or a related field, with 5+ years of experience analyzing data to answer critical business questions. Master’s Degree with 3+ years of experience or PhD also eligible.
Technical Mastery: Advanced knowledge of SQL is required. Proficiency in Python or R is a plus for building sophisticated optimization models.
Data Visualization: Experience with tools like Tableau, Shiny, or Streamlit to create impactful data stories for executive stakeholders.
Analytical Rigor: Strong understanding of experimentation and statistics (e.g., hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and statistical modeling) to analyze lead and feature-level performance. Experience with modeling and simulation capabilities preferred.
Cloud Platforms: Experience working within cloud-based environments such as AWS and Snowflake.
Strategic Thinking: Ability to handle operational complexity and move from “what” the data says to “why” it is moving, enabling data-driven decisioning for the entire organization.
Agility: Comfort working in a highly agile, intensely iterative environment where you must manage multiple priorities and ambiguous concepts.

How We Work

We balance creativity and innovation on a foundation of in-person collaboration. For most roles, our employees work three or more days in our Austin headquarters, where they have the opportunity to collaborate in-person, adding richness to our culture and knitting us closer together.

How We Reward You

Realtor.com is committed to investing in the health and wellbeing of our employees and their families. Our benefits programs include, but are not limited to:

Inclusive and Competitive medical, Rx, dental, and vision coverage
Family forming benefits
13 Paid Holidays
Flexible Time Off
8 hours of paid Volunteer Time off
Immediate eligibility into Company 401(k) plan with 3.5% company match
Tuition Reimbursement program for degreed and non-degreed programs
1:1 personalized Financial Planning Sessions
Student Debt Retirement Savings Match program
Free snacks and refreshments in each office location

Financial Crime Data Analyst

Division:
Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC)

Department:
Financial Crime Markets (FCMI)

This role is graded as: Associate – Level 8 – Regulatory
Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk.
Your internal recruitment contact is Isabelle Groves via isabelle.groves@fca.org.uk.
Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted.

About The FCA And Team

We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK.

SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition.

The Financial Crime Market Intervention department, within the Specialist Directorate, provides specialist expertise to help reduce the risk that regulated businesses are used for financial crime.

The department includes four Financial Crime Specialist Supervision teams, a Sanctions Supervision Team, a Fraud Supervision Team and a Risk, Data and Strategy Team. Working with colleagues across the FCA and external partners, it focuses on money laundering, financial sanctions, fraud, bribery and corruption. This role sits in the Risk, Data and Strategy Team.

Role Responsibilities

Help shape innovative data-led approaches that enhance the FCA’s ability to prevent and detect financial crime, protecting consumers and markets across the UK
Turn complex data into clear, actionable insights that support supervisory decisions and drive meaningful regulatory outcomes
Collaborate with colleagues across Data and Supervision to deliver impactful projects that enhance the FCA’s financial crime capabilities
Develop specialist skills in data analytics within a high-profile regulatory environment, building skills and experience that can help protect millions of consumers

Minimum

Skills required

Prior experience using Excel, SQL, or another data analytics tool to interrogate and manipulate data
Prior experience analysing data to answer defined questions and draw practical conclusions
Prior experience presenting analysis clearly in written, visual, or verbal formats

Essential

Effective communication skills, with the ability to explain data analysis and insights clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
Ability to deliver high-quality work to tight deadlines, using initiative and sound judgement
Well-developed stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build effective relationships, provide constructive challenge and confidently engage with senior stakeholders
Ability to prioritise competing demands and manage multiple pieces of work with minimal supervision
A collaborative and forward-thinking approach, demonstrating curiosity, innovation and a positive attitude to problem-solving
Confidence in making informed judgements, taking timely decisions and learning from experience to continuously improve outcomes
Experience creating data visualisation dashboards (e.g. Tableau), analytical programming languages (e.g. Python, R or advanced SQL) and knowledge of financial services, regulation, financial crime, or supervisory data is desirable
undefined

25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices
Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary
Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually
A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle

For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page.

Our values and culture

Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation.

If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support.
